review_text: 100% Achievement Review: Based on my experience completing all the (available) achievements. Feel free to follow my Steam Curator & Youtube Channel for more 100% reviews, videos & achievement content! Title: Skate. Summary: Multiplayer skateboarding game Personal notes: Skate. is an open world skating game set in a fictional city called San Vansterdam. This is the fourth installement in the Skate series, although they don't like to call it Skate 4. Before I start, I want to say that I grew up playing the original three Skate games and loved them. When I heard they were making a new one I was quite excited as it had been a long time since the latest game, being Skate 3 in 2010. Despite this "hype", and it being a free title I was left pretty dissapointed overall. Let's start with the good. The gameplay and skating mechanics are really well made and the main reason I love these games. It feels smooth and fluid, and hitting a solid line always feels rewarding. However, I dont credit it too much as we had these mechanics in Skate games a decade ago. I also think the multiplayer is implemented well and I appreciate rewarding teamwork. I am not the biggest fan of the artstyle personally but I can see what they were going for and It looks pretty good overall. That's about it for the good. For the bad we have quite a bit more. The gameplay loop is terrible and my biggest gripe with the game. You do these "daily" challenges which are normally the exact same day in day out. The reason you do these challenges are for rip chips/score, which you use to level up, unlock more fast travel points/challenges and customize your guy which leads me to my next point. Customization, In the old games we had so many choices for customization out the gates, In comparision to this one with barely any out the gate and all the brand items are pay-walled. Also why does a Skate game need a Battlepass and four different currencies in the first few months? Along with a store full of paid items, that shall I mention is above where you can get the free, less cool stuff. I understand microtransactions, especially being a free game but I dislike me being forced to look at it everytime. My next point is that this game, at least personally totally missed the Skate culture I knew this game for such as replacing Coach Frank with a robot voice. The fact that many game-modes are missing on launch such as Hall of Meat or S.K.A.T.E saddens me. On top of all of this, my game ran terribly. I crashed so many times regardless of the settings(RTX 4070S/AMD 5800x3D) and the friends I played with experienced similiar issues, almost to the point I wanted to give up hunting all the achievements. Achievement wise, most were pretty easy except two I listed below taking a lot of dedication. 11000 Rip score is quite the task, especially if they keep nerfing how many Rip Chips you get per daily challenge. Along with landing, not crashing with a combined hour of 4X score. All things considered, I don't really recommend this game currently in it's state. The skating is a blast and you can certainly have some fun with your friends for free but I would rather spend my time playing any of the other decade old Skate titles instead. Time it took to complete: 61hrs Most difficult achievement(s): - Every Trick You Skate (Spectated 50 other skaters.) - Fully Localized (Reached 11000 total Rip score.) - On a Heater (Kept a 4x multiplier going for a combined total of 1 hour.) Difficulty rating: ★★★☆☆☆ 6/10 Overall rating: ★★★☆☆☆ 4/10

review_text: listen, i love Skate, and this, by and large, is a Skate game. so while i don’t love this particular Skate game, i can’t help but at least like it because of my affinity for the series. now, is this an objectively good Skate game? in its current state, no — not at all. horrible physics, missing essential tricks (no finger flips, under flips, dark catches on launch, wtf?), lazy gameplay design, overly repetitive challenges, mobile-game graphics, shaky performance (regular framerate drops even on a solid pc, CPU constantly sitting at 70c, etc. meanwhile, Skate 3 ran at a near-perfect 60fps on the fricking PS3 while looking ten times better), and of course, microtransactions (i’m usually pretty agnostic about microtransactions, but only when i feel they’re a sensible element in a game. in a Skate game, they almost feel criminal, especially given the state this one’s in) bog ts way the hell down. i’ll give this a little leeway for being in early access, but i’ve got minimal trust in my favorite saudi prince–owned company, Electronic Arts, to make this substantially better by full release. maybe they will surprise me, but i doubt it. thank you for your attention to this matter.

review_text: Skate is an unfortunate tale of corporate greed wrapped in nostalgia. The original trilogy was beloved and defined by its authenticity, the culture, and creativity, which this entry has been revived not out of passion as the marketing deceptively says, but out of profit. This reboot of the series attempts to ride the wave of its predecessors while fundamentally misunderstanding what made them special. The game self labels itself as an early access title, which acts as a shield meant to deflect valid criticism. Yet somehow, despite being "unfinished" it already features a battle pass, four separate in-game currencies, rotating shop offers, and micro-transactions wazoo. The presence of loot boxes and time limited bundles says everything where the priorities lie. (The only feature of this game which I have never experienced any bugs in has been the store UI, go figure) What makes this whole thing sting even more is the contrast to the originals. The classic Skate games celebrated real skate culture, officially licensed clothing brands, professional skaters, a campaign that told your story of becoming a legend, and multiplayer built around friendly competition and creativity. This new version instead feels like a live service experiment designed to extract engagement and spending rather than evoke passion. Everything revolves around daily missions, often are the same exact spots every day, except yesterday it asked for a nose grind, today it ask for a crooked grind. This reboot isn't just disappointing, its disheartening. I grew up playing the original trilogy on my Xbox 360, I fell in love with the secret pro tapes, the grit of every slam and scrape, and picking my favorite board brand, whether it was Baker, Alien Workshop, Krooked, all without spending a dime extra. Those games made me want to actually go outside and learn to skate. Now it feels hollow. A series which once stood for freedom and expression of real skate culture has been turned into a monetized platform pretending to be a tribute. Until Skate and EA can find that soul again, this is a reminder of what we lost.

review_text: How to destroy a beloved franchise Ignore any and all feedback from players during the early playtests. Try to appeal mostly to fortnite fans, not skateboarding and skate game fans. Launch in Early Access and do Season Passes and microtransactions before the gameplay and world map are close to being finished, or even in just a decent spot. Have every Early Access dev update and patch focus entirely on monetization, currencies, and cosmetics rather than the core gameplay that actually matters. Build the worst and most boring skatepark city of a map in the history of the franchise over years of dev time, without the traditional variety and modes of the previous games that might make this blandest location possible even somewhat fun or grounded. When everything is over the top or designed explicitly for skating like any random skatepark, then nothing is unique or interesting. Launch with the only small district that's borderline normal unfinished, and then never finish it (Brickswitch). Mention no paywall to any gameplay content and maps up front as being a hard stance, then drop news of a slightly reworked tutorial map having a real money paywall and then later fake currency paywall. Every player could probably list a bunch of other things they personally care more about that they are still super bummed about, like the lacking online features and functionality, community parks, vert and transition and lip tricks and pumping and momentum still sucking, missing tricks, wonky physics and aids and lacking hardcore options, missing game modes. Even the visuals, character designs, lacking skate culture, brands and clothing, wear and tear, and whatever other nonsense that doesn't phase me much at all. Their opinions are still valid, though. Nothing in games is ever perfect, but Full Circle and EA have seemed to have completely missed the boat with this one and decided to speed run its demise after shoving out an unfinished game while also taking the monetization approach of a finished game, every decision they've made since putting it out there has been worse than the last. EA has more than enough funds to not be as scummy as they have been here, especially when it comes to something as dead simple as keeping their word on no map paywalls. They should have just taken the common sense approach and remastered the original games for all modern platforms with some upgrades and improvements (like being able to get off board and move and drop objects in the original skate.) as a classic collection, and then make a new skate game (or not) based on the how well that was received. Although I suppose if they had done that, the old fans and new fans would be even more disappointed with this new game if it turned out more or less the same as it currently has. Congratulations, and rest in piss to the skate franchise. You did not deserve this, but it's all EA knows at this point.

The customisation is bland and expensive; you'll often just get the same ugly item reskinned 20 times from doing the challenges. This game really shouldn’t have been released to the public with LESS content than almost every other skate game previous to it. There are no Hall of Meat challenges, which is a shame because I quite like the ragdoll physics in this game; they don't feel as stiff as the earlier games yet aren't as jelly-like compared to Session and SkaterXL. This game completely misses what skate culture even is; it's entirely corporatised with loot boxes, microtransactions and other forms of revenue. It's almost like this game is catering to a millennial audience who have never touched a skateboard in their life. Honestly, if I could give an in-the-middle review, I would, because if you don't skate in real life, this game is probably tons of fun and even if you do it does have some enjoyable elements. But as a whole, I hate the fact it's a live service game and would encourage people to play it but not give them any money as it sets a bad precedent for the future of the games industry.

review_text: I have played this more than 0.3 hours but it does not show since I played through the EA APP and also on the Xbox series x. This game feels less like a natural evolution of the original Skate series and more like a departure from what made those titles resonate with the skateboarding community. Instead of capturing the culture, grit, and personality that defined the earlier games, this new installment often feels disconnected from actual skateboarding and the people who love it. In the classic Skate titles, the world felt authentic. When you fell, your character got dirty, scraped up, and visibly worn down — details that added immersion and grounded the experience. The environments were gritty, full of graffiti, rough textures, and the kind of urban atmosphere skaters instantly recognize. Even the security guards added charm and unpredictability, becoming memorable parts of the gameplay loop. In contrast, the new game feels overly polished and sanitized. The world is clean to the point of feeling artificial, and it lacks the personality and edge that defined the earlier entries. One of the biggest disappointments is the absence of real skate brands. Iconic companies like Element, Zero, Blind, Baker, and many others helped players feel connected to the culture. Seeing a board you actually owned appear in‐game created a sense of identity and authenticity. Now, the equipment feels generic — almost like skating on department‐store boards with no real-world relevance. The challenges also fall short. They’re repetitive, uninspired, and rarely offer anything that feels genuinely fun or rewarding. Without meaningful progression, recognizable brands, or a world that reflects real skate culture, it becomes difficult to feel invested. Instead of celebrating the community, the game often comes across as a monetized product focused more on cosmetic sales than on delivering an experience skaters can relate to. Overall, it’s disappointing to see a series that once captured the heart of skateboarding shift toward something that feels more like a cash grab than a love letter to the culture. There’s potential here, but right now, it lacks the authenticity, attitude, and soul that made the original Skate games so memorable.

The monetization, the art style, the emotes, etc. - The game forces you to be always online. While it's not a dealbreaker for some, being repeatedly kicked out of the game because you couldn't connect to the EA servers is incredibly annoying. This bug has been "fixed" in every bug fix report in the past month, yet it keeps happening. - The map feels empty. The added verticality in season 2 just makes you feel like you're climbing for minutes, only to finish the line much quicker, usually ending in a bail, as the lines commonly end abruptly (Jumped off the last ramp? Nowhere to land, oops). - And lastly and most egregious is the monetization. By the price I would have paid on the deluxe welcome pack, I actually just bought a real life skateboard and some accessories. Overrall, the whole game just feels like a pg-13, sanitized and board-approved version of previous games in the series, with several features removed, repetitive daily challenges, lack of multiplayer features and added FOMO to drive up in-game sales (did I mention this game has up to 4 currencies?). As a big fan, I truly hope this is not the last hurrah of the franchise, and I wish they ported and updated the previous games. Even though Skate 3 is 15 years old, it still feels like a much more complete game.

review_text: I enjoy skating in real life as well, but I honestly suck at doing tricks because I’m too lazy to go through all the sweat and tears it takes to learn them. Just play skate. Pros: Engaging and fun overall, with a big map and plenty to do. Daily mission resets give you reasons to keep playing and chasing new scores. Cons: Doesn’t really feel like what the Skate 1-3 community was asking for. Feels clunky, overly modernized, and a bit unrealistic at times. A lot of pay-to-win style features, even though it’s still in Beta. Very buggy, with way too many issues. If you want the good-looking cosmetics for free, be ready to grind missions endlessly for cases. Part of the map still isn’t finished somehow. The AI NPCs need serious work or should just be removed. Genuinely, it’s a good game and one of my go-to games when I’m bored and just want to chill. It does get stale after a while, but at least it’s free.

review_text: Corporate Greed and Live Service models are a plague to modern videogames. The skating feels absolutely amazing and the parkour is surprisingly good, dare I say it's better than in most games that include parkour mechanics. If there's one thing that Full Circle absolutely nailed, then it's the gameplay. However... while this game plays great, it SEVERELY lacks in everything else. I may have said that the gameplay is great, however there's so much missing. Season 2 promises better handplants and impossibles, alongside an improved replay editor. Season 3 promises darkslides and new gamemodes. But that's exactly the problem, why are we being drip-fed content that was available in Skate 3 on LAUNCH? that game came out 15 years ago. We had more features in a game released 15 YEARS AGO. This is an issue with the live service model. In order to make it seem like we're getting "new content", they're just adding features that should've been in the game on launch. So many features are currently missing. What about game of S.K.A.T.E.? What about hall of meat? Why is it that we don't see an x-ray of our bodies when we fall from high up? It's all in the details. This game is missing a lot of them. But you'll get to experience those in a couple months time! Maybe if you buy the battlepass, they'll add stuff faster! But what do publishers love most? Money and Denying accountability. That's why this game brands itself as "early-access" However, if you sell in-game currency for up to 100€, Have a fully functioning seasonal system with battlepasses and 20€ cosmetic bundles, then you're not in early access. This is a fully released game, disguised as an early-access title in order to avoid any criticism. When it comes to visuals, they are extremely lackluster and lack STYLE. Usually I don't comment on visuals in a game, but with a skating game and Skate games in particular, you expect a certain tone and art-style. What at first (back in 2022) looked like a dirty, grimy, realistic looking skate game, now looks like Fortnite for the lack of a better term. It's extremely cartoony and unlike Fortnite, the customization leaves a lot to be desired. You cannot change the color of your clothes, you cannot change the position of your cap, there are no tattoos, you cannot color your hair with custom colors, there's next to no body shapes and I could go on. It's quite the paradox actually, because despite the game pushing so hard for cosmetics, there's not only a very narrow selection of them, but the quality LACKS. There's very few Boards, Grip colors, Grip patterns, Hoodies, T-shirts and so on. Cosmetics in the shop are extremely overpriced and rarely look good. The cherry on top, is that the vast majority of branded clothing/customization is paid. Most of the free branded items are either stickers or really bad looking clothing. On the topic of branded clothing and other customization related to real-life brands, why are there no real-life personalities? Where are all the pro-skaters? Why are the only characters in the game just voices, rather than actual people you skate with? And why does Vee... exist at all... which brings me to my last criticism. The dialogue & story in this game is genuinely horrible. First of all, why didn't we get a singleplayer mode for this game? Since there's no singleplayer mode, it's only a matter of time before the plug is pulled on this game and we will never be able to play it again. People who paid for cosmetics? your money is forever gone! Oh, you wanna play the game? tough luck buddy! it's an online-only game! Anyways, the "story" is just a bunch of tutorials one after another. there's like 2 characters alongside Vee that briefly describe what the current story (tutorial) mission you're doing, is about. The dialogue is whatever, but what totally kills it is the delivery. Every single character in this game, talks like a robot. The delivery feels so fake, there's absolutely zero emotion behind everything they say. It feels as if these voices were done by AI, which brings me to Vee. Vee is singlehandedly the most annoying part of the game. Not only is she terribly unfunny, can't ever shut up, but most importantly of all she's an AI. THEY LITERALLY PUT CHATGPT INTO THE GAME. What did Skate 3 have in place of Vee? Coach Frank. An actual person that skated with you in the game, and helped you get better. Coach Frank was replaced by a soulless version of ChatGPT. As of right now, changes are coming way too slow for people to care and people are dropping out en masse. However, even despite that, there's a chance for this game to make a serious comeback. Unlike a lot of other games, Skate. has a REALLY solid foundation. The core of the game is good, they just need to focus on adding content. FAST.

review_text: 2.5/5 So, the next entry in the Skate franchise is finally here after many years, and it's extremely weird. Pfftt, since it's still in Early Access, I'll go easy on it. Let's start with the art style. It's obviously a lot different from what Skate usually looked like, but I personally find it nice. The Sims 4-esque look of the characters and the colorful world really fits the skating aesthetic. I really don't like the techy look of the whole menu and how it always reminds me of those stupid loot boxes I have to claim, new items available in the marketplace and so on. It just feels soulless and corporatized. I've seen a comment somewhere that said "this looks like one of those crypto metaverse scam games", and I couldn't agree more. Another thing that is just really tacky is the dialogue. Developers, taking a random person and giving them skateboarding lingo doesn't automatically make it cool, like at all. The map is really decent and there are a lot of fun spots to land your tricks. Graphically, it's decent too. The lighting could be refined, and textures and environment details are just about okay, but I guess they're trying to make this lightweight for lower-end devices, so I'm okay with that. This is kind of where my first issue with this game starts. My PC runs this game extremely smoothly, until I join an online session. For some reason, the game just becomes laggy as hell, and it even stutters really hard at times. I'm guessing it has something to do with server syncing, but it's such a huge difference in performance that it makes me think there might be more issues besides that. And even then, the multiplayer just doesn't feel exciting. There is barely any player interaction. The mechanics feel really solid and it's clearly the highlight so far. It meets the demand for a fun skateboarding sim sandbox and it's really easy to understand the basics. The animations are smooth and the overall feel is just really nice, but damn there are many bugs. However, they seem to be the only thing that gives this game any kind of character, so I don't even mind them. I'm completely fine with a free-to-play model with loot boxes, but they're just really in your face all the time and it gets extremely annoying. I found the soundtrack to be really decent. I was pleasantly surprised when I heard some artists featured here, like Magdalena Bay, Denzel Curry, Car Seat Headrest, and so on. I would really rather have a choice to just pay for and play this game offline, freely enjoying these great skating mechanics and this nice world, instead of having to deal with this horrific server lag and forced marketplace pop-ups.

Multiplayer: The second big issue with this game is that there is basically nothing multiplayer wise to do. Parties are fine, except challenges are normally finished within 20 seconds cause I went for the 100% of this game. Some missing moves but I like the fluidity of the gameplay part of this game. As much as you can hate on every other part of the game, if they did not nail this it would have been dead on arrival. They did improve the system in this game, and the prop overhaul for this game made me actually use it, unlike skate 3's. I don't think it's something to brag about though and put moves that were in skate 3 in the game's road map. That's like saying a store change is a major feature. Again the thing you can compare this to is Halo Infinite. Free game that kills itself with greed, but overall a good game underneath all of the crud that's thrown on it. I just finished the 100% achievement for it today, hopefully when I come back something is added, but this game got bland after the 4th hour in or so. At the end of the day it is still free, so pick it up and ♥♥♥ around for a bit.

review_text: This Game has some fantastic PVP traits that I really enjoy and the gun customisation is industry standard as far as I am concerned. I've had some fantastic PVP in this game but there are some significant issues that I find distract from it:| - Art style and changes: I am unsure if I am just no longer the target demographic (and therefore they are focusing on non-western markets), but the games art style and focus is just weird. I don't care about zombies. I don't care about weird cross-overs with Cyberpunk - I like a grounded extraction shooter that has sim elements - a few steps down from what tarkov is. Whilst there is still this, several of the recent steps in the art direction and game direciton make it feel very confused and not something that that I relate to. Unsure if this is just because this is what is desired within asian markets. - The monetisation is absolutely rancid and predatory. I have no problems with supporting a game through microtransactions if it is free, but this requires the ongoing use gambling mechanics that generate neglible returns. Its possibly the worst implementation of microtransactions I have ever seen. If you want something that is easy, accessible - look at the Finals as a model. Its also incredibly hard to get access to the things you actually want - 70 Australian dollars for a skin? Yeah no thanks bro. - The cosmetics are rubbish: Even if I do manage to try and get access to some of the cosemetics, they are completely meh. Where are the grounded operator skins or weapon skins? I actually rather keep the weapons as vanillabecause of this. - The UI: THe gun customisation and UI in so many ways is industry leading, but other areas is really average. What are all these events? why do I randomly get gifted currency? I just absentmindedly click through them to get money and have no reason to care otherwise. Multiple sub menus are average. If you can deal with the above, then you have a good shooter. I myself have just found over time the art style and monetisation have pushed me away to go play games like Gray Zone Warfare as opposed to something like this. I hope this changes!

review_text: **Arena Breakout: Infinite — How to Turn a Potentially Great Game into Absolute Garbage.** It's honestly unbelievable how badly you can ruin a game that originally had so much potential. Arena Breakout: Infinite is a perfect example of how developers can take an interesting hardcore shooter and turn it into a complete Chinese-made disaster. **Balance? Apparently, nobody even bothered to test it. Game design? It feels like decisions are made completely at random. Logic behind the gameplay mechanics? Forget about it.** Instead of building on the game's strengths, fixing existing issues, and actually listening to the community, the developers seem determined to bury their own project. Every gaming session feels less like fighting other players and more like fighting the developers' terrible decisions. And the most frustrating part is that none of this feels like the challenge of a well-designed hardcore shooter. It's just plain bad game design. A game like this should reward tactics, experience, and smart decision-making — not constantly leave players wondering, "Who the hell thought this was a good idea?" **Arena Breakout: Infinite isn't becoming harder or more interesting. It's becoming dumber, more frustrating, and increasingly pointless.** It's amazing how you can have a solid concept, good technical foundations, and an interested player base — and still manage to screw everything up so spectacularly. The developers need to stop pretending everything is going according to plan and actually start fixing their game. Because right now, this isn't a serious competitor to other tactical shooters. It's just a poorly balanced mess filled with questionable design choices. **Final verdict: Another disappointment straight off the Chinese gaming assembly line. A game that could have been great but has managed to sink straight to rock bottom.** **Absolutely NOT recommended. Don't waste your time, patience, or sanity on this garbage.**

review_text: (English version available below) / (Английская версия ниже). ⚙️ Трезвый взгляд на ABI после 2000 часов в Таркове. Стоит ли играть? Cмог ли китайский гигант Tencent сделать убийцу главного экстракшен-шутера? Если коротко: Нет, не убил. Но заставил Буянова попотеть. Ниже разложу по полочкам, почему ABI - это одновременно глоток свежего воздуха и спорный продукт. 🟢 Что реально порадовало + Запуск за секунды. Загрузка в рейд идет секунд 30. Умер? Через минуту ты уже снова на карте в полной экипировке. Никаких «Ожиданий игроков» по 10 минут. + Игра не превращается в работу. Сюда не нужно заходить как на вторую смену. Захотел пострелять - зашел, кайфанул часик и спокойно вышел. Никакой обязаловки. + Нет тупых квестов. Нас избавили от маразма в духе «убей 15 ЧВК в прыжке с завязанными глазами». И главное - никаких квестов, которые тебя заставляют уныло перепроходить после каждого вайпа. + Читеров намного меньше. По моим ощущениям, в разы. Да, софтеры бывают везде, но тут они не встречаются в каждом втором рейде. + Античит работает на вас. Если вас всё-таки убил читер и его потом забанили - игра возвращает вам весь потерянный лут. Вот за это прям огромный респект разработчикам. + Игра не тормозит. Оптимизация на удивление отличная. FPS стабильный, картинка сочная, фризов в перестрелках нет. + Удобно играть. Человеческий интерфейс, понятная карта прямо в игре, нормальные маркеры. Не нужно держать открытой Википедию на втором мониторе, чтобы понять, куда идти. 🔴 Что напрягает - Донат. Да, игра бесплатная, но Tencent хочет денег. Валюту можно купить за реал, а безопасный контейнер дают только по платной подписке. Без доната на высоких уровнях копить деньги на топовый шмот будет тяжело. - Тесные карты. Локации довольно зажатые, из-за чего ПвП часто начинается в первые 20 секунд после спавна. Вас просто зажимают с двух сторон. - Меньше атмосферы. Игра ощущается как стерильный хардкорный шутер в стиле Call of Duty. Тут нет того подкожного страха и безысходности, как в Таркове. ⚖️ Прямое сравнение: ABI vs EFT * Порог входа: В ABI всё понятно сразу, обучение дружелюбное. В Таркове нужно страдать первые сотни часов, заучивая выходы по сторонним картам. * Работа игры: ABI летает даже на средних ПК и быстро загружается. Таркову нужно топовое железо, ССД и куча терпения. * Суть лута: В ABI всё упрощено - важна только цена предмета на рынке. В Таркове каждый болт, провод и туалетная бумага нужны для Убежища и квестов. * Боёвка: В ABI она более быстрая, динамичная и аркадная. В Таркове - медленная, позиционная, с тяжелой инерцией движений. * Прогрессия: В ABI ты просто играешь в свое удовольствие. В Таркове игра заставляет тебя упарываться в гринд квестов ради торговцев. 📣 Итог Arena Breakout: Infinite - это качественный, быстрый фастфуд. Если у вас мало времени после работы, вы устали от багов и хотите просто зайти и пострелять - игра идеальна. Она бесплатная, так что попробовать точно стоит. Но если вам нужна глубокая атмосфера выживания и вы готовы ради этого терпеть боль - Тарков остаётся на своём месте. Для бесплатного проекта — крепкие 7.5 из 10. Если обзор помог определиться - закиньте лайк или награду, буду благодарен! ⚙️ A sober look at the ABI after 2000 hours in Tarkov. Is it worth playing? Could the Chinese giant Tencent make the killer of the main extraction shooter? In short: No, he did not. But he made Buyanov sweat. Below I will break down why ABI is both a breath of fresh air and a controversial product. 🟢 What really pleased me + Start in seconds. Loading into the raid takes about 30 seconds. Died? In a minute, you are back on the map in full gear. No "Player Expectations" for 10 minutes. + Play does not turn into work. You don't need to come here as a second shift. If you want to shoot, you go in, enjoy an hour and calmly go out. No obligation. + No dumb quests. We were saved from insanity in the spirit of "kill 15 PMCs in a jump blindfolded." And most importantly - no quests that make you sadly replay after each wipe. + There are much fewer cheaters. According to my feelings, at times. Yes, there are softers everywhere, but here they are not found in every second raid. + Anti-cheat works for you. If you are killed by a cheater and then banned, the game returns you all the lost loot. For this, a huge respect to the developers. + The game does not slow down. The optimisation is surprisingly excellent. The FPS is stable, the picture is juicy, there are no freezes in the shootouts. + Easy to play. Human interface, a clear map right in the game, normal markers. You don't need to keep Wikipedia open on a second monitor to figure out where to go. 🔴 What is stressful - Donation. Yes, the game is free, but Tencent wants money. Currency can be bought for real, and a secure container is given only with a paid subscription. Without donations at high levels, it will be difficult to save money for top clothes. - Cramped maps. The locations are quite tight, which is why PvP often starts in the first 20 seconds after spawning. You are simply clamped on both sides. - Less atmosphere. The game feels like a sterile hardcore shooter in the style of Call of Duty. There is no subcutaneous fear and hopelessness as in Tarkov. ⚖️ Direct comparison: ABI vs EFT * Entry threshold: In ABI, everything is clear at once, the training is friendly. In Tarkov, you have to suffer for the first hundreds of hours, memorising exits on third-party maps. * Game Operation: ABI flies even on average PCs and loads quickly. Tarkov needs top hardware, SJS and a lot of patience. * Loot essence: In ABI, everything is simplified - only the price of the item on the market is important. In Tarkov, every bolt, wire, and toilet paper is needed for the Vault and quests. * Combat: In ABI, it is faster, more dynamic, and more arcade-like. In Tarkov - slow, positional, with heavy inertia of movements. * Progression: In ABI, you just play for fun. In Tarkov, the game forces you to grind quests for merchants. 📣 Conclusion Arena Breakout: Infinite is a high-quality, fast-paced fast food experience. If you don't have much time after work, you're tired of bugs, and you just want to go in and shoot, the game is perfect. It's free, so it's definitely worth a try. But if you need a deep atmosphere of survival and you are ready to endure pain for this, Tarkov remains in his place. For a free project, it's a solid 7.5 out of 10. If the review helped you decide - throw a like or an award, I will be grateful!

review_text: This game had every ingredient to be the extraction shooter that honest players could actually call home — and the devs wasted it. Let's start with the most obvious rot: cheating. Not casual cheating. Organized, commercial cheating. There are entire supply networks — storefronts, Discord servers, subscription services — openly selling hacks for this game. Speed hacks, ESP, aimbot, full suites. The cheating infrastructure is so mature it has customer support. I've spent time identifying these accounts, studying their behavioral patterns, even tracing the supply chains back to the sellers. You know what the devs have done with that information? Nothing that matters. The anti-cheat is cosmetic. A system that can be bypassed by suppliers who've clearly had months — if not longer — to reverse-engineer it. Bans happen slowly if at all, and the accounts come right back. The developers know this ecosystem exists. They benefit from it passively because cheaters keep buying the game, keep buying Bonds, keep fueling the economy. Banning them aggressively would hurt the bottom line, and that tells you everything you need to know about where the priorities are. Then there's the economy. The vault storage system is designed to squeeze you — permanent upgrades tied behind grind or cash, with E-Box "rentals" that disappear at season's end. The game is structured to make you feel like you're progressing while actually running in place, and the Koen economy is balanced around the assumption that a percentage of your lobby is cheating and extracting more than should be physically possible. This could have been something real. The extraction shooter genre is starving for a game that takes its player base seriously. ABI has the map design, the tension, the moment-to-moment feel of something that works — and then you run into your third rage-cheater of the session and remember what you're actually dealing with. The devs aren't struggling to fix this. They're choosing not to. There's a difference. Don't waste your time or your money here. The house always wins, and in this case, the house is also selling aimbots. To the Devs: Apologizing while not addressing infrastructure is not zero-tolerance. Zero tolerance means storefronts with 50k+ sales and 24/7 support don't exist openly. They do. That's not an "ongoing battle" - that's an unaddressed market you pretend not to see. Funny: my emails got zero response, but a review turning buyers away gets a PR reply in a month. You didn't find conscience - you found a revenue threat. Save the performance for someone who hasn't watched you ignore documented cheating operations. Since your "commitment to improvement" - I came back. Took your survey. First game? Empty map, just AI. Second and third? Died to aimbot/walls. Two of three. Nothing's fixed. You're not "limiting cheat effectiveness" - you limit email replies to what hurts your wallet. The house still wins. You just don't like players counting cards (they have now hidden this review.)

review_text: I really enjoyed ABI during my first 50 hours. It was the best extraction shooter I've played. Unfortunately, the more I played, the more the game started to disappoint me. What I Like 1. The Loot System The loot system is excellent. You always know exactly what you've picked up and how much it's worth, thanks to the clear value and color . It makes looting quite satisfying. 2. Gunplay and Weapon Selection The gunplay feels great, and there's a wide selection of weapons and attachments to play with. That said, the current so called meta means most players use the same 5 guns. 3. The Feeling of Security If you die with a 1 mil kit at the start of a raid, i would be fuming. However, unlike many other extraction games it's relatively easy to get Koen again. Between the different free Gear/Money rewards, you're rarely left completely broke. 4. No Pay-to-Win While I think the skin prices are absurd with a dumb gacha system, the game itself isn't pay-to-win, which deserves credit. That's becoming increasingly rare in free-to-play games. What I Dislike 1. Solo Nightmare The game constantly caters to four-man squads. The solo mode is a complete joke since you can only play two maps, and there are no Normal or Lockdown modes. Auto Match? Nope. It doesn't work. I've tried countless times to queue with Auto Match enabled, but it rarely happens. The game desperately needs a proper solo mode. 2. Arcade Direction Lately, it feels like it's moving toward a more arcade style direction with increasingly over the top skins that don't fit the game 3. Events ABI has an ungodly amount of ongoing events at all times, to the point where I don't even know if I'm playing the same game anymore. 4. Gear Balance Armor feels useless at close range, but as soon as you get 1 meter out of effective range, your bullets feel like they do nothing. There are only about five guns worth using. You can also bring high-tier ammunition into lower-level lobbies, which is an unfair advantage in my opinion. 5. Cheaters The cheating problem has gotten really bad. I constantly get instantly one-tapped in the head, and then I watch the kill cam only to see someone tracking me through walls. And reporting feels useless Conclusion I genuinely enjoy ABI when I'm playing with friends. The core gameplay is fun, the extraction mechanics are solid, and the loot system is the best in any extactin shooter so far i played. However, when I play solo, the game becomes incredibly frustrating. Between the lack of solo options, awful balancing, and the increasing number of cheaters, the experience quickly becomes negetiv. The game has so much potential. And it's great in many ways but I think it's heading in the wrong direction.

review_text: I started playing ABI in the middle of S1, and it felt like a realistic extraction shooter. Unfortunately, every new season pushes it further away from that identity. The matchmaking is terrible: T6 players with thermals are regularly paired against players running budget kits. Gun balance has also become a mess! Fights no longer feel realistic; it often takes entire magazines to down someone, while weapons that should be devastating (like the Mosin) can require multiple headshots just to do meaningful damage. The game increasingly feels like an arcade shooter rather than a tactical extraction game. Cheating is another huge problem. Most cheaters receive only temporary bans, return quickly, and players who lose expensive gear get no compensation or rollback. The monetization is also hard to justify. The game is free, but many cosmetic bundles are around $100+, and instead of military-themed gear, the game is filled with anime, cyberpunk, fantasy armor, swords and other unrealistic cosmetics. Honestly, the only consistently impressive part of ABI is the graphics, if you have a powerful enough PC to run it. Every update makes the game heavier and more demanding while the gameplay quality keeps declining. Rating: 2/10 - great graphics, but poor matchmaking, bad weapon balance, rampant cheating, and a complete loss of the realistic atmosphere that made the game popular in the first place.

review_text: At the time of writing this review, I have logged nearly 900 hours, constantly running red raids, actively moving around the maps, and mostly playing in duos or full squads, Throughout my time in the game, I have successfully extracted with over 1 billion worth of loot, killed nearly 2,000 players, and dealt over 1 million in total damage. I know almost every single spawn point on every map, and I am fully familiar with various tactics for close-quarters combat or pushing any point of interest. Here are my conclusions for anyone thinking about starting this game or considering a return: ABI is an utterly unrewarding, toxic, suffocating, and tedious game that will repeatedly mock you until you completely lose all hope. Why? Let's break it down: 1. TTK (Time to Kill) It is abysmally fast. It doesn't matter if you are wearing a 3+ million kit (including top-tier ammo, grenades, and consumables) with a fully modded meta weapon, or if you are running naked with a literal pipe instead of a pistol — the outcome is the same: you will die in a split second. Addition to this point for clarification: TTK shouldn't require you to dump multiple mags into someone, but it should be high enough for your armor to actually do its job — surviving maybe 15, 20, or 25 bullets (as a rough estimate). To be clear, I am talking about T6 armor specifically, the absolute best gear in the game. When T5 ammo shreds a T6 plate in a split second, it is completely absurd, considering the ammo is a whole tier lower than the armor. I could understand dying that fast if the enemy was using a hard-hitting rifle like the FAL or MK14 loaded with T6 ammo, but that's not the case. Barely anyone even runs those rifles anyway because of their insane recoil, and despite the guns being cheap, T6 ammo is just ridiculously overpriced. 2. Armor The most useless and overpriced thing in the game. No body armor or helmet will ever give you enough time to react, turn around, and return fire if you get caught off guard. Even if you somehow survive the initial burst, your armor durability shreds instantly. This leaves you with zero competitive edge, forcing you to either rush to exfil immediately or sit in a bush waiting out the entire raid just to survive. Even T4 ammo from an H416 can melt you in seconds. 3. Playing Solo? Forget it. If you don't have friends or prefer solo raids — don't even bother. This game hates solo players; it doesn't recognize or reward them in any way. In squad matches, you will constantly face the knockdown mechanic (if you don't instantly finish an enemy, their teammates will just revive them) or squads with perfect info on your location thanks to teammate markers. As for the dedicated solo modes, you get a rotation of just two maps a week. The first is massive and wide open with forests and hills, where you can randomly catch a single red bullet from a bush. The second forces you to check absolutely every corner, otherwise, you'll die to some rat who has been sitting in one spot for 20 minutes just waiting for you. 4. Broken Economy High-end gear is unjustifiably expensive. Finding the rarest "red" items in a raid will barely cover half the cost of your top-tier kit (or just your T5 ammo supply). Meanwhile, purple and gold items are worth pennies. The loot drop rates in Lockdown raids are terrible. Unless you kill other players (and pray that their gear is worth at least half of what you brought in), the game turns into a tedious looting simulator just to break even on your ammo costs. 5. Loot & Playstyle Want to know the most consistent way to make money I've found? Playing like an absolute rat. You sit quietly, listen, sniff out all nearby points of interest while everyone else is fighting, and then swoop in to clean up the leftovers and grab some free T5 armor or guns. And even if I die, the most I lose is around 450k... Reminder: I am writing a review for an extraction shooter, not a scavenging simulator. 6. Cheaters Cheating is a disease in many online games, but in ABI, it’s an incurable cancer. The developers completely ignore it and seem incapable of doing anything. Don't believe me? Just look it up on YouTube or TikTok. There is a massive amount of cheaters literally making content out of this. One streams it live, another shares how they see a cheater with ESP or aimbot in almost every single raid. They don't get banned for weeks — sometimes months. Because of this, you will constantly run into: Players who always know exactly where you are. Players who land perfect, flawless headshots. Players who will laser-spray you right in the neck (the most vulnerable spot) using T3 ammo on a trash weapon while you are wearing top-tier gear. The game's website has an "Inspector" role for players to review reported gameplay demos, but even that helps absolutely nothing. Recent Updates Want to know what they added recently? A new mode with literal superpowers/abilities, and a couple of new guns just to simulate variety among top-tier weapons, while half of the rifles and SMGs in the game remain completely unviable. Not to mention that weapon modding has become completely standardized into a single meta template, killing any real variety or experimentation with different attachments. Every project has its pros and cons, but this game's pros are so minor that they simply cannot compete with the cons. Essentially, once you hit level 30, you've already seen all the content. You won't find anything new after that, except for various glitches or ways to climb into unintended, out-of-bounds spots to get an unfair advantage. Summary What is the final verdict? It's a looting simulator with elements of surviving against cheaters. The weapons are only there to give you the illusion that you actually have a chance to kill someone.

review_text: As a player with over 1,000 hours in Escape From Tarkov, I accidentally stumbled on this game while going through ETF withdrawals during the (ongoing) repair of my computer. Desiring the same extraction PVP fix, albeit without the requirement of 64GB RAM in order to enjoy the game (my laptop has a mere 16GM RAM), I decided to give this free game a shot. Already, I can tell you it improves on every pain I didn't even know I had with EFT. Specifically, First, A MAP. I get it, EFT is is about hyper realism. But I ended up playing EFT with multiple maps/guides/ands other sources open, to include Pestily's YT walkthroughs, which ended up with an even higher unofficial ram requirement. Instead, ABI says "here is your map". Second, it was bad enough having gear fear; but EFT's gear entropy was something else, making every round (especially for a non-cheating, life having player like me) as a stressful SNAP BACK TO REALITY of trying to balance a budget. ABI eliminates durability/entropy gating mechanics entirely. Third, while I get trader-gating content, it ultimately just felt like a grind for the sake of a grind, since a cheater can easily get good gear no matter what - by cheating and winning. At least I immediately had access to decent gear for sale INSTANTLY in ABI. Fourth, if you are an Edge of Darkness EFT player, you got ♥♥♥. Just putting it out there. Fifth, there is a casual PVP mode as opposed to unescapable sweat mode. More clearly, you can essentially choose your level of PVP engagement, starting at normal, where players exist - so the threat is real - but they are sparse enough that you aren't getting instagibbed at spawn (most of the time lol). Sixth, the history of this game - removing the P2W of the past - shows the creators actually LISTEN to their fanbase. Which is exactly the opposite of Nikita and EFT. I could go on, but I would like to get back to playing. As a busy Dad of three, husband of one, and a humble guy who doesn't have the money to replace his old gaming rig, it is so refreshing to find a game that both respects my time and my budget. Even after my PC repair is completed (taking forever, Thanks ALLSTATE WARRANTY) I'm not sure I'm going back to EFT.

First the positives: -easy to pick up -easy gun customization -easy Call of Duty-esque get back into action quick playstyle -nice graphics -nice sound design: overall sound design not talking about footsteps in particular -good variety of maps and loot the in-between: -player driven economy -relatively decent exploration even outside of the main POIs -ability to play what you like -"tiered" progression -satisfying loot experience (more prior to recent update now not so much anymore further detail in the lower section) the bad: -directional audio: it's buggy sometimes, esp when it comes to elevation changes -gunfights: this gets picked up in the next section further down so look there for an explanation -current looting experience: since the latest update you now immediately know if an item is high in value or not bc high value items now take longer to be identified compared to regular items the ugly: -cheating: yes they ban cheaters, yes they have an anti-cheat, does it stop ppl from cheating? well ofc iit does not, every MP game will have that problem and i am fully aware of that, the problem here is that your loadout is on the line so if you have a high value loadout you're much more likely to store it then to use it or you play iin secure-ops where you can't lose your loot -economy: some players have millions upon millions if not billions extracted, you get to keep you money past "wipes" so those players have an immediate advantage over new players and can diictate market prices, yes the game does combat that somewhat by giving out tier 4 gear like candy but that doesn't help against artificial inflation of ammo and gear prices esp above tier 4 -gunfights: Part 1 PVE: like i said above, the point returns, why? Bc it fits both categories, gunfights against bots are by enlarge mundane and more nuisance than challenge, i get it just like in Arc Raiders the bots are supposed to be a nuisance that you have to take into calculation for gunfights and can use as an asset, the only exception to this are bosses and the additional spawns alongside them as they usually carry higher tier gear, react faster etc. i'm not saying bots should be as overpowered as they are/were in Gray Zone Warfare but i wish there would be different tiers of AI and esp the AI in TV-Station, inside Armory and inside the Hotel on Northridge could def pose more of a threat than they do now. Part 2 PVP: gunfights in PVP are insanely hit or miss, either you get matched with people with full Tier 6 armor, H416 or Mosin with Tier 7 ammo, usually in a duo, trio or squad stack or you get matched against people doing corpse runs i.e. standard kit, no helmet <200k loot value, no in between, the former you will not win against nor will they lose any money while "risking" their gear bc their friends will just pick up what they had on and exfil right away, the latter you prob spend more money than you gain, this is by no means exclusive to ABI but it somehow feels unfair nonetheless -matchmaking: if you're a new player who just started out and you get matched against seasonalnolife557 with 20bn extracted tell me where the balancing is, one risks his loadout with the potential of going broke while the other sits on stacks of cash throwing one Mosin with full red ammo and 50 slot backpack filled with nades and stims into the raid one after another without a care in the world part of the experience? review_text: Here is a brief assessment of my take on Abi. First, let's cover the basics needed to actually enjoy the game. Do you speak Russian? Do you have enough real money to spend? Are you willing to use hacks? Do they have no conscience when it comes to the spoils?I’ve been playing ABI since the beginning of Season 3, and I’ve experienced quite a few fun days along the way. Anyone who plays the game—or even just watches a little YouTube—knows the BDC (Inspectors). The current season is defined by the fact that, out of roughly 30,000 active players, about 20,000 are cheaters who aren't playing legitimately. The remainder consists of players with over 500 million in their stash who are more interested in stealing others' loot—or complaining when it happens to them.Since I mentioned the Inspector program: I’ve been at the highest rank since Season 4, and I have an 89.87% accuracy rate when it comes to spotting cheaters. The result this season is that—unless you happen to be an elite shooter player—you’ll frequently run into a cheater who quickly takes you out and teabags you. Experienced players generally show little interest in taking new players under their wing—except perhaps to treat them as a source of loot or as bait. Even when you do find someone to play with, it rarely lasts, because the game tempts you to relive the good old days of CS.Insults are the order of the day; putting someone down is a form of affection; and flaming—when you die yourself—is the way of saying "you suck."It feels like this game is populated almost exclusively by English speakers or Russians. Which brings us back to the topic of the good old CS days: insults no one understands and, far too often, all-out hostility. The support is a marvel in itself; a few tests suggest that if you’ve spent money on these games—and I mean over 100 bucks—you’ll actually get support. That applies if a cheater kills you, or if your teammates kill you just to take your loot. You do get back the money you spent on gear or loot, but if you think you can play the game without actually spending money, you’re in the wrong place. Besides, there isn't really a good reason to spend money—unless you want to die while wearing a "good-looking" skin.Basically, it’s always the same story: unless you get lucky or are willing to spend a long time figuring out the system, you’ll struggle to make any progress—or won't get anywhere at all. The community is worse than in CS, because we’re playing a loot-extraction shooter here where money is the ultimate measure of everything.And when it comes to loot, many people know no bounds. The Maps Some maps can only be played in specific ways; for instance, if you pick the "Armory" map, you pretty much have to be a "rat" who can or wants to snipe—which is considered the worst way to play the game, since everyone whines if you actually play like a real sniper.Or they have plenty of grenades with them, or they’re using a good wallhack and aimbot. Far too often, the match turns into a pure grenade war decided simply by how many grenades each side is carrying. Valley is a map that anyone can play right from the start; the problem with it, however, is that long-time players know tricks to bypass the maximum gear score limit, allowing them to bring in superior gear or ammunition.When you play this map, you quickly get the feeling that it’s just a hunt for newbies. You do manage to get some good loot now and then, but you have to realize that you can lose it all just as fast because experienced players camp the exits. TV Station TV Station is a map designed purely for PvP if you want to make money fast—or risk losing everything—this is the map for you. It is small, fast, and brutal. People always say it plays really well, but a major problem—especially in the current Season 6—remains the presence of cheaters and YouTube sites advertising undetectable cheats for sale. Most long-time players have a very high stash value and, consequently, a lot to lose. And the worst part is simply that many people have now adopted the mindset that hate, insults, and flaming are the way the game is supposed to be played.

review_text: Pros: The Best Way to Lose Friends This game says it’s Free to Play... they lied. It costs friendships. You think you’re just dropping in with the boys? Nah. You’re dropping into emotional bankruptcy. One second you’re all laughing; the next, Chad "accidentally" forgets to cover your flank and your million-dollar kit is gone. Now you’re broke AND you hate Chad. This isn’t just a shooter; it’s a social experiment. Arena Breakout Infinite doesn’t just test your aim—it tests your ability to forgive betrayal, cope with digital poverty, and resist the urge to uninstall Discord. GG devs, you’ve created the first truly "Pay-to-Lose-Friendship" game. 10/10, would get betrayed again. Cons: A Identity Crisis in Progress I’m writing this as an extraction veteran and a "Tarkov refugee" who genuinely loves this game. Initially, ABI was everything I wanted: stable servers, great QoL, and a fair chance for average players to take down "sweats" with a well-placed shot. Unfortunately, recent updates are stripping that identity away. The "Effective Range" Problem: The balance has shifted from skill-based to stat-based. I recently headshot an unhelmeted player with an FAL (T4 ammo), and they survived because of the "Effective Range" mechanic. A flat -30% damage penalty just because a player is 1 meter outside an arbitrary range feels arcadey and punishing. It makes it nearly impossible for a budget player to win via skill. The "Sweat" Shield: The introduction of craftable self-revives and injectors that reduce limb damage spread has removed the only weakness of T6 "juggernauts." By trying to make the game more "casual-friendly," the devs have actually made the "sweats" unkillable. You now have to win the same fight three times just to confirm a kill. Economic Stagnation: Without wipes, the economy is inflating rapidly. The gap between the "rich veterans" and new players is becoming a canyon. Expensive weapons are often non-viable in the current meta, yet their price remains high, leaving new players with no path to compete. TL;DR: The game is losing its hardcore soul by trying to be "overly casual," but in doing so, it has only made the rich players more powerful. Please, devs—stop taking pages out of the wrong books. Return to the tactical, lethal roots that made this game a breath of fresh air.

review_text: Arena Breakout Infinite nails the feel of a hardcore extraction shooter tight gunplay, strong audio design, and high stakes raids that genuinely get your heart racing. On a mechanical level, it’s solid, and when everything clicks, the tension rivals the best in the genre. Unfortunately, it’s weighed down by aggressive monetization and progression systems that constantly undermine that experience. Gear disparity, grind heavy progression, and pay to skip elements make deaths feel less like a learning moment and more like a punishment designed to push you toward spending. In a genre where fairness and risk reward balance are everything, that’s a big problem. There’s a good game buried here, but right now it feels like potential held hostage by design decisions that don’t respect the player’s time. If monetization and progression are reworked, this could be something special but as it stands, it’s hard to recommend unless you’re already deeply invested in the extraction shooter formula.

review_text: After returning to Arena breakout from its Beta/season 1-3 and joined back mid season 6, I have to say this game has actually gotten better overall. Now to be said there are still flaws, however 90% of the criticism it is receiving is not actually part of the game or genuine issues. Recently they added zombies, this is getting a bit of backlash due to "It no longer being a realistic shooter and now its just another arcade shooter." First off, if you played beta, or even kept up with story line, this has been teased, and part of the story for a while, so "zombies" were to be expected. With that said, they are not that bad, they look good, move good and sound good. HOWEVER, they are redundant, there is not anything special about them. Overall its just a wash. I like them, they are not that bad, however I see the complaints. Another one is the removal of hostile Sector. This is honestly the only bad change this update. There are MANY players that play for pure PVE alone(I am not one of them so idc, but I will miss it) Hostile sector was a challenge for most, and actually required skill and time. It also filled that missing spot for PVE players. Yes there is still PVE but its only the endless zombies, or No mans land. No mans land would be fine, if it were challenging or intense. However you can just waltz through like its nothing, and you cannot go into it for free if you run out of passes. Cheaters, still a problem, like any game, however in 90% of other games, they do not get noticed because you are not truly effected by them, you just die and respawn or lose and invo of loot(Like rust or DayZ). This however you lose a lot, and its much harder to fight cheaters. However in my 120+ hours since I started playing again, I've ran into 2 cheaters. This is all in lockdown or forbidden zone as well. They are a problem, and always will be, just as any game. We can only hope their Anti cheat or catching process gets better to catch them more and faster. (also to help prevent) The people complaining about PVP. Idk wtf they are on about. PVP this season was saved. No more armor piercing RNG, no more pointless headshots or bullets just ricocheting off the helmet. Yes time to kill went up, but its a better thing, it allows the worse players a chance to outplay, or gives the better players rewarding good aim (headshots etc). ITs also such a small amount, but its so much better not getting one shot by a T4/T5 bullet while wearing full T5/T6. For anyone that wants to check this game out but gets worried about the reviews, take them, including this one, with a grain of salt. Try it out, only you can decide if you like it. Personally, I do love this game, it runs great, feels great. Its a blast, and I enjoy playing it even when I get ♥♥♥ on. right now its a solid 8.5/10. I would highly recommend checking it out. **I played about 50+/hrs on their original launcher before steam release**

review_text: It's good. If you never played Tarkov, that game is a great entry point to semi-realistic extraction fps sub-genre. Definetly not for everyone, might be tough to learn, but the learning curve is very interesting. Some cons, that worked for me: -UE5 game, that works well(although, you might get some fps-drops, when moving towards big compound, but they rarely affect the game) even on my 4600h rtx3050m. -It's something new. It was my first entry to this sub-genre and at first, i didn't know anything about those kind of games and it managed to deliver me emotions, i always looked for in shooters. -The thrill of combat. You'll stress out a lot. And you WILL like it. -Even inspecting weapon makes a sound. I learned it the hard way. -Gunplay is good. -The constant questions and desicions the game forces you to make: "Do i hear bots, or real players?" "Should I go out and loot some more or should I secure my own equipment?" "Oh god, im stuck in this room and I hear a squad outside" "Ha, it's just a bot, nothing to worry abou-" "My squadmate died, how do I get out of this situiation? Oh no, i hear them coming for me, God help me please, I'm scared" "♥♥♥-♥♥♥-♥♥♥, i'm bleeding, in pain, my limbs are broken, and my character is heavely breathing, WHAT DO I DO" and after several hours, after dying so much, when the stars align, and when enemies make a mistake, you might get a "♥♥♥, I KILLED EVERY ONE OF THEM AAHAHAHHOIAHJOAEIJG" - and this is what no other fps shooters have never delivered. -Skirmishes here are pretty much realistic: Knowing basic CQC might help a bit and is really ♥♥♥ cool to exequite Firefights could be methodical, but they are mostly chaotic and nervous You will naturally want to send an enemy all your grenade stash you have before going in/out It's more pressuring when there are no sounds of an enemy. You might die because you weren't lucky enough(e.g. you have 3 tier armor but some rich ♥♥♥ really went with 4T bullets on white-tier farm/you went with full 4T armor but some broke ♥♥♥ with 3T bullets pierced through your helmet on white-tier farm) Single wrong decision might lead you to death and you make a lot of tactical decisions during enemy contact. Much-much-much more different and fun experience with friends. It's better to not look at any guides, just go in fully blind and try it out.

review_text: 👍 Recommended TL;DR: A streamlined version of Escape from Tarkov with close to none technical issues, faster progression, and a much smoother onboarding experience. The game heavily rewards coordinated squad play, making solo play significantly more challenging at higher levels. While I don't personally like the more arcade-like direction the developers have taken recently, it's ultimately a matter of taste. Tarkov vs. Arena 👍 Where it shines; - It's free. Unlike Tarkov, you don't have to pay to find out whether you'll like it or is it gonna run on your pc with 256 Gigs of ram and 6G connection. - Much easier to learn than Tarkov thanks to features like an in-game map, simplified healing, and a more accessible UI. - Weapon and gear customization is available after roughly 10–20 hours instead of being locked behind hundreds of hours of progression. - Gearing up for raids doesn't take longer than the raid itself, everything is at reach and user-friendly. - No friendly fire, making it much easier to team up with random players. - 800 hours played with zero crashes or major bugs, which is genuinely impressive. - Stable servers and a much smoother online experience compared to Tarkov. - Faster-paced PvP with greater freedom to rotate, reposition, disengage, and coordinate thanks to visible teammates and cleverly designed maps and areas. - The new PvE mode is an excellent addition. You can play solo, with friends, or through matchmaking, and the AI feels challenging without being unfairly aimbot-like. 👎 Where it falls short; - Solo play becomes extremely difficult at higher-level hence not enjoyable, Expect to face coordinated premade squads. flanking and outplaying multiple opponents is much harder than in Tarkov. - Recent updates have pushed the game toward a more Call of Duty-style experience, and the general direction of dev is CoD like extraction shooter experience, this will not satisfy those who value realism. - Colorful cosmetic skins undermine the gritty extraction shooter atmosphere, talking about which, you don't really feel an atmosphere of hardcore harsh environment in-game. - Severe damage drop-off at range and heavily reduced one-shot potential encourage close-quarters squad fights over long-range engagements. Some players will enjoy this faster-paced style, while others may find it disappointing and arcady. - Character and weapon animations are noticeably worse than Tarkov's or many other decent shooter games, and can feel like mobile game. This is one area where the developers should invest much more. - The meta is much more restrictive than in Tarkov. High-level gameplay tends to revolve around the same few weapons and gear loadouts, making matches feel repetitive, whereas Tarkov offers a much wider variety of viable guns, ammunition, and attachments. Verdict Arena Breakout is one of the most polished extraction shooters available. It removes much of the frustration associated with Tarkov—technical issues, excessive grinding, and poor accessibility—while keeping the core tactical extraction gameplay intact. That said, the game has gradually shifted toward a more arcade-focused experience. If you enjoy fast-paced, squad-oriented action, but don't mind it being arcady, you'll probably love the current direction. If you prefer slower, more realistic gunfights with stronger emphasis on long-range engagements and hardcore atmosphere, you may be less enthusiastic. I would easily recommend this game to anyone interested in extraction shooters who doesn't mind it being a bit arcady, whereas I would seldom recommend Tarkov to someone new—not only because of the initial grind, but also because of its seemingly endless and random technical issues which hardly ever gets fixed. Rating: 7.5/10 Now if you'll excuse me, I'm going back to Tarkov so I can remember why I wrote this review.

(You might think it's because of the ping, but to date, ping hasn't been a factor in those kinds of deaths). - The game's killcam is broken. review_text: I've enjoyed Arena Breakout until now, but adding a PP-19 skin with "Z for Victory" engraved on the weapon is a terrible decision. There are countless ways to create military-themed cosmetics without referencing real-world political or military propaganda. I hope the developers remove or redesign this engraving. Until then, I cannot recommend supporting the game.

review_text: There is a TL;DR at the end. I have spent more time than I would care to admit on this review, but I put in the effort because FragPunk is actually a good game that seems to be in the wrong hands. This review was originally roughly twice as long, but I had to cut a lot because of Steam’s character limit. ✅ SHARD CARDS ARE ABSOLUTELY THE HIGHLIGHT OF THE GAME Shard Cards change how the rounds function and really set FragPunk apart from its competition. They can give you anything from small benefits in the background, such as damage and fire rate increases, to large changes that completely affect how you approach the round. For example, "Blade Master" is a card that gives you a sword that blocks bullets from the front, forcing enemies to shoot your feet or your back. ✅ GREAT CHARACTER DESIGNS, SKINS, AND COSMETICS The character designs are genuinely good, and the higher-tier skins are very high quality. They are similar to the expensive, higher-tier skins in Valorant. They look good, have good animations, and the sticker system is nice as well. Unfortunately, you cannot view most skins in-game once they leave the store, so newer players may only discover them by seeing other players using them. Some skins eventually return, but there does not appear to be any guarantee about when or if a particular skin will come back. ✅ SOLID GUNPLAY FragPunk is similar to Valorant and Counter-Strike in terms of its objective, map design, and general gameplay. However, it doesn't have a counter-strafe mechanic, and its guns have consistent recoil patterns. This means you can memorize and learn to control the recoil patterns. ✅ GOOD MAPS Most of the maps are good and work well with the game’s Shard Card system. They have their own identities, and the gameplay is generally fun across most of them. ✅ SURPRISINGLY FUN SIDE CONTENT FragPunk also has side modes such as Toy Front Line and its related modes. They combine tower-defense elements with a Call of Duty Zombies-style survival mode and mix in mechanics from the Shard Card system. You survive multiple rounds, place defenses, and earn some pretty decent cosmetic rewards. The mode is fun for a few hours, but it becomes repetitive. These modes can become truly great if developed a bit more. I'd also like to highlight that COD zombies started as side content as well. ✅ SOLID RANKED SYSTEM The ranked system is generally fine. It may be a little too easy to rank up, but I have seen worse systems in other games. Reaching the highest rank is still satisfying, and the rewards are fine, even if they are nothing crazy. It is good enough and serves its purpose. ❌ ROUTE FLAPPING AND CONNECTION PROBLEMS I am not sure whether this is a server or routing issue, but some players constantly experience something called route flapping. It causes severe lag and can make the game practically unplayable. I personally do not have this problem, but I have friends who experience it, and I have seen other players complain about it as well. Even after extensive troubleshooting, it sometimes refuses to go away and only seems to happen on FragPunk. ❌ THE CHEATING PROBLEM IS COMPLETELY OUT OF HAND This is easily the biggest problem with the game and the main reason I will probably stop playing soon. It feels like everyone is cheating, especially once you reach Diamond and the higher ranks. I am not only talking about players using aimbots or wall hacks. Cronus Zens, no-recoil macros, scripts, and similar forms of cheating appear to be everywhere. Almost nobody seems to have recoil. In Diamond, it is common to see what appears to be half the lobby cheating. In Ace and Punk Master, the two highest ranks, you would be lucky to find even one player outside of your party who appears to be playing legitimately. It is that common for nearly the entire lobby to be using scripts, no-recoil macros, or similar cheats. The cheating is not subtle either. Players can openly admit that they are cheating and still not get banned. I have personally had several players argue with me that using no-recoil macros and scripts is completely fine because “everyone” uses them at the higher ranks. I reported those players and it always turns up nothing. I want to emphasize that these are not just players with good recoil control. They can use the guns with the most recoil in the game, yet their reticles have absolutely no bounce or movement. There is not even the slightest amount of give, and they never seem to make a mistake while controlling the recoil. Their aim can be terrible in every other way, but the reticle still remains perfectly steady. If you're like me and have played a lot of shooters, achieving the highest ranks in them, and learned how to control recoil, you can tell the difference. What these players are doing is not consistent with legitimate gameplay. Their recoil control looks like world-class talent while everything else about their gameplay suggests otherwise. Some people try to call these “legit cheats” because you supposedly still need to be good at the game. To put it in plain English, using no-recoil macros or devices in a tactical shooter is cheating, and you are not good if you need them to perform well. ❌ REPORTS SEEM TO ACCOMPLISH NOTHING When you report someone, you receive a message saying that an investigation will begin shortly, but nothing ever seems to happen. I have reported close to 30 blatant players over the past two or three weeks without receiving a single notification that action was taken. ❌ THE ACTIVE PLAYER POOL IS EXTREMELY SMALL At the time of writing, FragPunk has 344 Steam players online, a 24-hour peak of 897, and a 30-day average of around 600, compared to its all-time Steam peak of 113,243. The game is also bleeding roughly 100 to 300 average players each month. The console population does not appear much larger, since the in-game scoreboard regularly shows balanced or mostly PC lobbies. This small player pool means repeatedly encountering the same people and cheaters at higher ranks. ❌ THE MENUS ARE A NIGHTMARE The main menu is an absolute nightmare to navigate. There are a million different menus, pop-ups, events, currencies, and icons constantly being thrown in your face. It is not intuitive at all, and you may need to play for actual weeks before you can quickly find everything. ❌ THE MEMBERSHIP SYSTEM Characters cost 18,888 Gold each and take a long time to unlock through normal gameplay. This grind clearly exists to push players toward the membership system. The monthly membership costs $9.90 and includes the Premium Battle Pass and access to every character, but only while the membership remains active. The annual membership costs the equivalent of $8.33 per month, paid upfront, and includes the Battle Pass. Its main benefit is permanently unlocking every current and future character, even if you never renew the membership. ❌ THE MONETIZATION IS RIDICULOUS FragPunk has loot boxes called Curiosity Pop Cans that can contain featured knife skins. The skin has a 0.01% overall drop rate, while the 100-material reward has a 0.99% drop rate. A skin costs 1,000 materials, and an Ultimate drop is guaranteed every 50 cans, meaning you could potentially need 500 cans to earn one. Buying that many would cost around $706 before tax, even after including the one-time discounted seasonal bundles. No cosmetic should cost anywhere near that much. ⭐ FINAL RATING: 6.5/10 Even with all of its issues, the most important part of any game is whether it's fun and has good gameplay. FragPunk is very fun. It is genuinely a great game, but it has a lot of significant problems that ruin the actual gameplay experience and drag it down. This game easily has the potential to be a 9/10 and could possibly even be a 10/10 in the right hands. TL;DR: A great game inspired by CS and Valorant, ruined by cheaters and bad Eastern monetization.
