review_text: As of writing this, the main story is officially over (or the current chapter at least) I've completed all side/world quests, main quests, event/guide quests, defeated all bosses/enemies (that so far are unlocked and in the game) at least once, some 100+ times. All without paying any real money and here are my thoughts and opinions on it: - as you can see all the game can be completed in about ~ 30 hours. - it is BORING BEYOND IMAGINATION. - Love the whole social features tho! emojis, stickers, emotes, chats, less restrictive filters than your typical games, more freedom, pictures, trade center, guilds, parties, guild center and objectives to achieve with the help of all of your guild members. (I probably won't be playing again or anymore but for other players... don't change this! this is cool! this is nice!) - so far there aren't really any "pay-2-win" and monetization feels fair and understandable. ### MOVEMENT ### - very choppy, i hate it. - sprinting does not feel any faster than walking speed until you get used to it. - EVEN THE DEVS KNOW some of the movement abilities are annoying so they just put a "deactivate" button for some skills/upgrades which is the equivalent of "it's not a bug, it's a feature!" - the quadruple jump, wallride, glide and flight is a pretty cool mechanic and fresh which is nice but omg the wallride is the most annoying movement mechanic of the game even tho it's pretty useful. ### COMBAT ### - cool visuals (could be improved but still cool looking) - sometimes enemies bug out and it doesn't play the attack animation so all of a sudden you lose 5k HP (this is not a performance issue, my pc is quite beefy) - combat in general does not feel satisfying or good, some classes (stormblade) feel like you're doing negative damage and instead healing some enemy types. ### UI & BEGINNER-FRIENDLINESS ### - beginner friendly... sure! but not always!!! (Ex: trying to figure out how to leave the homestead. [You have to press "P" btw.]) - UI... it's an asian game with hints and resemblance of certain gacha games which means a sht-ton of options, buttons, pages just to make it unnecessarily confusing. so there's that. - the active HUD... it's okay i guess. ### STORY ### - the story is unbelievably boring and uninteresting. - the dialogues and texts for all quests will always play out the typing animation and you can't just click to view the whole thing, read it then onto the next sentence like in most visual novels or narratives. so you're forced to stick through the whole thing OR completely skip the whole story. - there are some black screens with text to tell you whats happening in the story or in between which are completely unskippable and some of them have a very long duration which i find annoying. Even Lost Ark's Google-Transleted, omega-cringe story is far superior to this game's story. ### - Do i recommend it??? i mean it's nice with friends. - The community... idk i didn't interact with the community much so cant say whether they're nice or not. - there's also some talk about kernel-level (system-level) anti-cheat which is never a good thing to hear. - and incompatibilities with linux. Otherwise, it's very boring and i personaly will not be coming back. GG's Shanghai Bokura Thanks for... nothing honestly idek it was mind numbing throughout the experience...

review_text: After spending around 61 hours in Blue Protocol, I can confidently say this is the first game in a long while that's managed to keep me hooked every single day. I keep catching myself thinking about it even when I'm not playing which honestly says a lot about how I'm immersed to it. Visually, the game nails that Sword Art Online-style anime aesthetic which I've personally ALWAYS wanted in an MMO game. Exploration is genuinely rewarding which reminds me of the satisfaction I get from games like Wuthering Waves or Genshin Impact which is finding chests and coming across unexpected minigames keep exploration fresh and worth the effort. The dungeons and 20 player raids give off Final Fantasy XIV mechanics. They can be structured, cooperative, and they're unique. To me, this is the kind of experience that keeps me excited to queue for next ones playing with others. As for the time-gated systems, they're completely fine by me. I appreciate them since it keeps the pacing balanced and prevent burnout. The best part is it never feels unfair. You can still progress at your own pace and there will be new content that comes in small, steady chunks that keep the game feeling active and fun to come back to. Overall, this game has become my comfort MMO. The only one I open when I just want to relax, explore a bit, socialize with people and forget about the world for a while.

review_text: After being a day 1 player with now over 400 hours into this game, waiting for a bunch of content updates or even just events to do, now I can fully say the game at the moment as it is from the start became boring really fast. The dungeons feel unrewarding and monotone since its just 6 same dungeons in literally just different difficulties where they just bump up the needed DPS and the damage of the mobs. The time gating makes no sense for Life skills, leveling classes or life skills is simply just a pain to do since you always get interrupted by needing so many resources or focus points per day. Its build like a typical mobile gacha where you are just trapped in an endless cycle of doing dailies and then just logging out since the content is dry and repetitive. Actually investing time into grinding and improving your ability score feels like its locked behind a p2w wall if you want to keep up with the people demanding for you to be high level in new content. End game content is to farm the same 3 dragons in different difficulties, while the needed group of 12 or 20 people is just arguing if someone makes a little mistake and then you just struggle for hours trying to find people over and over again, cause someone left, just to clear simple easy content of a game that really isn't THIS hard. The social aspect of this game is in my opinion as well very little. Sure you can chat with people but actually doing content together is as well just boring repetitive dailies. At the start of the game the tutorial of life skills was talking about a trading system were people could trade to each other making the "social experience" better, just for it to be taken away a day after the launch. Being unable to trade makes most of the Life skill stuff feel even less rewarding and boring. On top of that again, doing harder content with other people is also frustrating just by the way this community has the shortest fused players I have ever witnessed. One slip up and you can P out of the dungeon requeuing with a new person. I had high hopes for this game at the launch and it seemed fun from what it was before the content just dried out fast and all of the leveling just felt like a chore without any fun. Which some of the pro's I can state are: -the character customization is nice, it lacks some individuality like voices and more face options but other than that it's actually really good. -Combat of this game is really enjoyable in my opinion. For an MMO I like the real time combat and the ability to dodge it makes it fun and feels more immersive in battle. Other than all of this a lot of improvement could be done to the game. I wouldn't be so harsh on this if the game actually felt like you don't have to reach for your wallet to be able to do stuff in it, after you finish the, at the moment mediocre, main story.

review_text: I really wanted to give this game a chance. I’ve wanted to play Blue Protocol (the original) ever since the first trailer dropped. I even played the Japanese version because I was so excited about it, and I was heartbroken when it was announced that it would be shut down. Then Star Resonance was announced. I followed everything closely and tried to stay up to date with all the information. However, I feel that streamers who played the CN Beta and CN version gave us too much hope — or rather, too much cope — for this game. Here is my honest positive and negative feedback: Positive Feedback The world feels great. The larger map in the first area (compared to the original Blue Protocol) feels exciting to explore, and the new additions are genuinely good improvements. New class: Verdant Oracle. This is something I would have loved to see in the original Blue Protocol. It’s a full healer class with a great design and enjoyable skills. Movement and traversal. The jumping and flying mechanics are fantastic. They make exploring the world fun and add a lot of freedom to movement. Color wheel customization. Having a color wheel for character creation, clothing, and more is a great improvement over the old system. Social aspects. The guild system and in-game social activities are well done, and they genuinely encourage interaction between players. Negative Feedback Character creation. The character creation options were heavily reduced compared to the original. While a few new hairstyles were added, many features were removed. I would honestly prefer losing the color wheel if it meant bringing back the more varied body sizes. Also, the original version included “voice choices,” which are missing here. Megaserver issues. If you want to run a megaserver for EU/NA and other regions, this isn’t the way to do it. The lag is severe for many countries, and the timegated content is unfair — players in some regions have to log in during work hours or in the middle of the night to participate. Event and activity times are only shown in one timezone (UTC-2), instead of displaying the player’s local time or at least including an in-game clock. Story quality. Oh boy — the story is a mess. Streamers claimed it was “better” than the old Blue Protocol story, and I highly disagree. It feels short, lifeless, and rushed, with too many black screens and white text instead of proper animation. The pacing is all over the place, and the grammatical errors are constant. The original story was engaging even though I didn’t understand everything — but this one? No thank you. Grammatical and translation errors. I’m convinced the translation was done by an AI — and not a good one. The amount of grammatical mistakes is overwhelming, and I’m tired of poor translations in games that ask for real money. Pay-to-win systems. The pay-to-win elements are far worse than they were ever presented. The developers even admitted in the CN version that they placed Skill Books in the Auction House directly from the GM side to keep things “in stock.” But the only players who can afford to buy these in bulk are whales. And that’s not the only problem: materials for Imagines can be bought with Bound Rose Orbs, which can be endlessly converted from normal Rose Orbs — because GMs are also putting endless Bound Rose Orbs on the market for conversion. This is unacceptable. Honestly, I would have preferred the rumor about botting over learning that the staff themselves are responsible. The “give us feedback” situation. Since the CBT, APlus has said they wanted player feedback to improve the game. We — the players — gave that feedback, with many posts getting 200+ votes in their Discord section. There was even a dedicated thread for grammatical errors. Yet, to this day, none of this feedback has been properly addressed. No corrections have been made to the reported translation errors, and there has been no acknowledgment of any major player suggestions. I don’t mean that things haven’t been implemented — I mean they haven’t even been discussed. We still don’t know whether any of our feedback is being considered at all. I’m deeply disappointed in this game. As long as the negative points I’ve listed are not properly addressed, I won’t be spending any more time playing it. EDIT course to the response from the APlus Team: If you are genuinely committed to resolving these issues, where are the updates and fixes for the translation errors? What is the current status of the ongoing megaserver problems? Up to this point, we have only seen maintenance announcements and new gacha content. The game has been out for nearly a month, and none of the easily addressable issues have been fixed.

I have reached out through the official Discord, submitted a support ticket, and contacted support directly through the website. The only response I have received is the suggestion to uninstall and reinstall the game. I have already done this. I have also attempted logging in on a different device, using a VPN, and verifying the game files. None of these steps have resolved the issue. At this point, it is clear that the problem is server‐side. My character is stuck in a corrupted cutscene instance, and the only resolution needed is for support to either relocate my character or reset the associated quest flag I was able to find a work around as I never heard anything back from the ticket I submitted so thankfully my character was recovered.

review_text: First off , amazing art style, truly the graphics are great, the land, the characters, it's all beautiful. The music is also good. One silver lining of Tencent having bought the IP is that amazon is no longer publishing it, which means you do get to create a loli for your character, so that's also fantastic. The character creator itself is also pretty good, doesn't have a ton of features, but still good. The story is... something, the one thing I can say is that our characters backstory mystery does seem interesting, but that's it, for the actual main story it's awful, it's horribly paced, feels way too fast, there's even a death with a little bit later a montage of the character and the time we spent, but we barely spent much time together, it needed WAY MORE before trying to hit us with that, and with the awful pacing, the payoff just isn't there. It also is super fast, within 10 hours total gameplay ish, you're already max level and the story is done, as far as season 1 goes at least. Barely 40% of the map explored, honestly it happened so quickly I was dumbfounded, I truly didn't expect to have already finished the s1 story. At least the characters seem cool, though speaking of, that's quite a nice main menu they have, I have no ♥♥♥ clue who half of those characters are supposed to be, you only meet like 3 or 4 of them in the story, is it all side quest stuff? Is it supposed to be player characters? I have no idea. The combat is cool, animations are alright, and enemy design is actually pretty nice. Though at points the combat feels buggy, heck in one boss fight during the Tribe section it was insanely buggy, I couldn't hit the boss, I think I needed to do something else, except I couldn't there was nothing else to do, and then I had no cooldowns so I could spam my ult, then I couldn't heal except then I could and it fully healed me, I honestly had no idea what was going on, eventually I managed to beat it, though I've no clue how. The movement is cool, 5 jumps is nice, though hovering up in midair cancelling ALL forward momentum is complete trash, actual garbage, feels terrible, glad you can turn that off. Speaking of movement, the mounts also feel slow, despite the fact they're not, it feels a lot better just using your 5 jumps instead. For the bad , besides 90% of the stuff above, there's also the fact that it is quite buggy, for example the quests for the Tribe section , I needed to interact with an NPC, except this NPC was inside some sort of stone brazier or statues or whatever, which I suspect may be part of the Christmas decoration, given that in cutscenes it was buggy showing me a POV from inside, so I couldn't see anything and also much earlier it showed an NPC clipping through a Christmas tree, clearly the devs did not pay attention to WHERE they were putting it, and just adding it wherever they felt like it, with no care for due process. Speaking of cutscenes, TOO FAST, a wall of text would appear and then disappear before I could read it, heck it happened multiple times besides just the black screen with text. Besides that there's also the cutscenes that would appear out of nowhere, last 3 seconds and end, like HUH??? That was barely anything. In general it was buggy though, like in one I'm floating in the sky with the unloaded terrain below me half there, half not. Attack indicators are terrible, half the time I can't tell if I'm taking damage or not unless I look directly at my HP bar. The minimap is super laggy for some reason. I know I spoke of the montage above after the character death but the most depressing fact was that Airona was supposed to be singing during it, yet there's nothing, much like the rest of the game, 70% of it or so doesn't have voice lines, so it was just background music with a dumb sepia tone montage that is not deserved as not enough time was put, sorry to talk about pacing again but damn, it really is awful. The money is super scarce, this one might be a skill issue but like, for example Unbound and bound luno, as if a premium currency with bound and unbound versions wasn't enough... Like to use the auction house you gotta spend Luno UNBOUND, as a posting fee or something, but to get Luno UNBOUND you need to sell stuff in the auction house, except you can't, because that STILL NEEDS LUNO UNBOUND, that one might be I simply don't know where to actually get it, besides using UNBOUND premium currency to buy it, as that's one way to do it. Besides that you need bound Luno to level up your skills, I was broke most of the game, I still have no idea what the ♥♥♥ to do about that, quests barely give anything, it must be selling but idk. This is probably part of the pacing issues, but by the end of it, as I stated above, I was max level which is 60, I'd rather less xp and more main quests, because that would mean MORE lore, better pacing, and hopefully a better feel. This is honestly depressing to see that this is what became of Blue Protocol... Overall , it's a beautiful game with a good character creator... That's it. review_text: This hit me with an unexpected wave of nostalgia. The atmosphere, art style and soundtrack feel like something I've experienced before, turns out, I kinda have. It's got that old soul, reimagined in a smoother, more accessible form. Technically it impressed me. The game ran incredibly smooth on my device with stable FPS, no input delay and good optimzation for a cross-platform title. The combat feels responsive and flashy enough without overdoing it, and loading transition is half-seamless. From a software perspective, I deeply appreciate the engine-side efficiency. However, I feel like the netcode could use stronger client-side prediction. Menus are also messy as there's too much information stacked on top of itself. Then there's too much currencies (GACHA SLOP) Monetization system feels bloated and unintuitive, like multiple systems were stitched together without unifying logic. Enemies and Bosses also lack behavioural complexity. Once you read their patterns, combat gets repetitive. Music is stunning but environmental sounds and SFX often overpower dialogues. PC performance is above average but mobile still suffers from inconsistent frame pacing and thermal throttling. Storywise, it's a mixed bag because it starts strong which feels cinematic, kinda emotional with that classic "you're chosen by fate" tone but it progresses surprisingly fast, skipping over emotional beats that deserved more weight. Then suddenly, it slows down again with long exposition and filler-style quests. It is both draggy and rushed, which sounds weird but fits. Some plot points resolve too quickly, other lingers too long. The world map is beautiful but lacks the depth or substance to make you feel its history. I found myself caring the vibe more than the story itself (pretty, nostalgic but surface-lvl) There's a potential here. It just needs tighter pacing and more emotional grounding which I'm looking forward soon.

review_text: This free-to-play title delivers a refreshing change of pace. While some progression can feel drawn out, the beautiful art style and satisfying combat make up for it. It’s a decent game overall—so let’s take a closer look. Graphics: The art style is distinctive and beautifully executed, offering a refreshing visual identity. Combat animations and graphical details across the board are impressive and enjoyable to watch. Unfortunately, the game is capped at 120 FPS. While that’s acceptable for this genre, the difference between 120 and 360 is noticeable—higher frame rates would certainly enhance the experience. Still, it’s a visually striking game overall. Audio: The sound design is excellent, with strong voice acting and impactful combat audio. Interestingly, while the text can be switched to English, all spoken dialogue and audio remain in the original Asian language, requiring players to rely on subtitles. It’s an unusual localization choice, but not a dealbreaker—overall, the audio experience is impressive. Controls: It’s straightforward to pick up and play, much like most MMORPGs. Game-play and everything else after: It’s a free-to-play MMORPG, which sounds great on paper. And yes, you can explore the world with friends, tackle dungeons, and take on some quests together. But I stress some, because there are frustrating moments where certain quests throw you into solo instances, locking your friends out entirely. Why it’s designed this way is anyone’s guess, but it does undermine the whole “play together” vibe. Thankfully, once you’re past the questing phase, the endgame opens up and that’s where group play really shines. There’s a huge variety of skills and talents to unlock, letting you shape your character however you like. You’re not locked into any one path—there are (I think) nine distinct skill lines, each with its own visuals, mechanics, and roles across assault, defence, and support. You can switch between them freely, which is a big win for flexibility and experimentation. Now, about XP... brace yourself. Yes, there’s a ton of XP to earn—but it’s a grind, and I say that with emphasis. You’ll see missions boasting “1 million XP in minutes!” but when a single level demands 20 billion, those numbers start to feel absurd. Same goes for currency: you might have 2 million (not called gold, but you get the idea), yet upgrading one item could cost 600K. It’s a game of inflated stats—everything’s big, flashy, and often misleading. That “250 million XP reward” sounds amazing until you realise you need 600 billion to level up. You get the picture. The map is vast and full of activities—dungeons, trials, raids, bosses (including world bosses), plus farming, mining, alchemy, and more. But remember that XP grind? It applies here too. Levelling up in these side systems takes serious time and effort. Menus... menus everywhere. Navigation can be a headache. There are layers upon layers of menus, and finding what you need isn’t always intuitive. Thankfully, the game uses orange exclamation marks to flag things you can redeem or check out, which helps a lot. Still, it’s a UI jungle. Customisation? Deep but confusing. There’s loads of cosmetic and gear customisation, but unlocking certain items can be a puzzle. The currency system is especially messy—four main types, each tied to different mechanics. Some items require real money, others need farming, and some (like Meowlux premium cards) cost 950K each, and you might need 15 or more. It’s a lot to track, and not always well explained. Expect to spend a fair amount of time running back and forth—but thankfully, the game offers some clever navigation features to ease the journey. Traversal is genuinely enjoyable, with unlockable abilities like mounts, gliding, and dashing layered on top of your standard character skills. These world-based movement options add a nice touch of flair and freedom. Slightly more playful tone: Yes, there’s a lot of running around—but the game throws in some neat tricks to keep it interesting. Auto-navigation helps, and the traversal abilities—like mounts, gliding, and dashing—add a fun layer on top of your regular skills. It’s a nice mix that makes getting from A to B feel less like a chore. It’s a fairly enjoyable open-world MMO. The quests are well-designed, missions are plentiful, side content is abundant, and the various runs offer a good dose of fun. Conversational and casual: It’s a fun open-world MMO—at least to a certain extent. Quests are solid, there’s no shortage of missions, side activities are packed in, and the runs are genuinely entertaining. Slightly more critical but fair: While not perfect, it’s an enjoyable open-world MMO. The quests hold up well, missions are everywhere, side content is dense, and the runs keep things lively. Standard gear progression applies—basic gear does the job, but stronger sets offer better stats and performance. You’ll be farming for upgrades, and if you’ve played any MMORPG before, you’ll know exactly what to expect. Would I recommend the game? Yes, it's a free to play MMORPG with some little differences and nice art style, worth a go at no cost to be fair.

review_text: It's free, and it has some cool elements, so try it out (I'd recommend with at least one friend, coms are important) Pros: - Tactical/Strategic - Large map, lots of players, tactical game that requires observation and positioning. - Sniping - This game hits all the right notes for a sniper, the feel of sniping in this game really is top tier. - Destructible environment - this is by far one of the best mechanics of the game, that separates it from other BRs. - Potential - This game has a lot of potential, however - in the BR - they need to make it competitive, unfortunately bloom, and latency issues ruin that. Cons: - Latency - You'll attempt to grab something from a box, it will give the animation like you succeeded, but then you realize you don't have it, and have to to turn around and press it again (hope there's not an enemy watching while you fumble with the crate) - Bloom - This just means when you aim, your crosshair is perfectly on a stationary target, you can still miss. - Ping System - Try to ping something, but it won't show until a few seconds later, or it won't ping at all, the audio queue of a teammate pinging an enemy that is next to you isn't even noticeable. It makes it so that, if you don't have full team mics, the game is miserable. (Just copy Apex Legends ping system, it's the best in the genre) - Audio - A tank will roll up on you and you won't hear a thing. RedSec for the first time is a really bad experience. You open a crate and it would flip upside-down, you'd try to grab a gun out of a crate, looking directly at the gun, but it would pick up the grenade next to it. Then you'd try to pick up a gun, and it just won't register, so you have to press it a few times (hope there's not an enemy looking at you at the time). The audio is terrible, a tank will roll up on you and you won't even hear it. The ping system is the worst part of the game, which is surprising, seeing as this game was made LATER than Apex Legends by years, why are we regressing? Let's add that there's bloom, which means when your crosshair is directly on your target, you will still miss randomly (Imagine - you're the last alive, everyone watching, you lock in, the enemy is in the open, you aim PERFECTLY, but you still miss, and then you die) All-in-all: Great game that has a lot of potential, I've had a lot of fun times in RedSec when I have a team of players with mics. The strategies that we can come up with are endless. But solo queuing? It's a disaster. If you don't have at least one other person (I'd recommend a full team) then the solo experience is just, better, on other BRs. Until they fix their ping system.

review_text: Rating: 👎 Not Recommended Hours Played: Enough to know better My RTX 5070 is putting in overtime rendering Fort Lyndon in crisp 2K at 165Hz, which is genuinely fantastic because it lets me see in ultra-smooth high definition exactly how my bullets are actively avoiding the enemy. Battlefield loves boasting about "Tactical Destruction" where you can blow up entire buildings, yet my highly trained soldier is completely paralyzed by the concept of a waist-high garden wall. Mantling over obstacles feels like you're trying to climb out of a swimming pool filled with wet cement. Gauntlet mode is admittedly kind of cool, but the main Battle Royale experience is just looting for 15 minutes before getting instantly evaporated by an F/A-81F Super Spectre from the new Top Gun event that you couldn't even hear coming. Save your SSD space. The only thing this game successfully destroyed was my patience.

review_text: Please follow United Critics for quality reviews Battlefield 6 & REDSEC Review About the Game Battlefield 6, like the previous games in the series, is an epic, cinematic, and intense shooter taking place in the modern era. Its combat can at times feel like straight out of a movie, and is unlikely to leave you disappointed. It contains: • A Campaign, which took around 6 hours to beat on normal difficulty, playing at a normal pace with a decent story, but might leave more to desire for those who would like to see more flushed out characters with more personality, and the story essentially being the usual West vs East, with a bit of a twist towards the end with who is behind the story events. • Multiplayer, which is, of course, the main attraction of the game, with plenty of different maps, both small and large, but not quite as big as 2042’s, a decent variety of weapons, which there will be more of as the game receives more updates, and 4 classes, which return from the older entries. There are, at the moment, about 8 different modes for multiplayer, but there is also the Portal, allowing for custom matchmaking • Redsec (Battle Royale); An intense and fun mode, bringing a ton of fun as well as frustration to the game, with some interesting mechanics, as well as some you would be familiar with if you have played Call of Duty Warzone, or other similar battle royale games. It brings missions, which grant you rewards upon completion, ranging from weapon drops, custom weapon drops, which also get dropped naturally as the match progresses, guaranteed “call-ins”, such as air strikes and artillery barrages, UAV, and Vehicle keycards, which can be an absolute terror to deal with if you aren’t appropriately geared to deal with them. About Redsec As is the norm with battle royale, the zone shrinks slowly over time, but unlike in most others, hitting the border of the zone results in an instant death, rather than being able to run around on the outside of it to maybe bide your time. Running near the edge of the zone causes you to very slowly lose health over time, which makes it important to outrun it to be able to regenerate health, as you will often be fighting near said edge, meaning your health won’t regenerate if you are running while also fighting near it, while also leaving intense moments where a teammate is dragging and reviving you as you are only a meter away from the zone, as your screen is turning red and scorched from the flames. The map is quite big and is good overall, but I would have liked to see more urban environments, as most of the map feels quite open. There are no self-revives, meaning that if you are downed, a teammate has to pick you up, or you get sent to the respawn screen. Every match has a second chance, where you will always respawn after your first death, even if you and all your teammates die, but only for a certain duration of the match, when it gets disabled, but you can attempt to return your teammates to the fight at any point via redeploy stations, where you can revive teammates, but need to stand next to the point for around half a minute if you are by yourself, and faster if you have more teammates with you. The redeploy stations make a lot of noise tho, and are marked for all enemies on the map to see that someone is reviving, so it can be risky if there are enemies nearby, and the station can only be used once. The same goes for certain missions, as there are some that make a lot of noise while you have to stay nearby to defend them from possible players trying to stop you. If there are nearby enemies, you can also perform counter-missions, which mark the enemies' objectives for you, allowing you to destroy them yourself and claim the rewards, or wait to try and ambush the enemies. There is also a cool mechanic, where lootable crates can contain weapon kits, which allow you to upgrade the weapon relating to the type of kit they are, normally between weapon recoil control or mobility, magazine capacity, or scopes. Each class has its own specialty in the mode, just like in normal Multiplayer, but what they are is changed for Redsec. The mode overall is great fun, especially as it’s free, and don’t be deceived by negative ratings, as most of them aren’t related to gameplay, but issues like mission progressions for regular multiplayer, which I believe have been changed as of writing this review. I would say my biggest gripe with Redsec is vehicles, more specifically, Tanks. Tanks are fun to use, and aren’t difficult to take out, but can be very unfair to face if you aren’t equipped with the right gear. When there are nearby tanks, the game spawns in Anti-Vehicle drops, which make it easier to deal with the tanks, but they are also too quick and easy to be repaired by Engineers, countered by the tanks having very limited ammo, which can be replenished on stations. As someone who has been on the delivering and receiving end of them, it’s conflicting on whether they belong in the mode or not, especially as in Quads (4-man squads), if a squad gets lucky enough with missions, they can claim up to 4 tanks for themselves, which I have come across and is a nightmare to deal with. Despite these issues, the game mode is definitely recommended for everyone to try. About Multiplayer The multiplayer is intense with small and big maps, as well as various modes where you can play as infantry, vehicles, or a mix of both. There aren’t a lot of maps at the moment, but there is a decent enough variety, with more to be added at a later date. Like the usual Battlefield games, there are 4 classes as mentioned for Redsec split between Assault, Engineer, Support, and Recon, each with their own specialties affecting weapons, and what they can do to support the team. Visuals The game looks visually impressive, and runs pretty well on mid specs on a mix of medium and high graphics (RTX 3060, I9-10th gen, 32GB RAM) with practically no performance issues at any point, other than the second mission of the campaign, where the game, for some reason, runs pretty poorly. Pros and Cons Pros A very fun free-to-play battle royale mode, Good variety of weapons Epic and cinematic Decently-designed maps Cons Lack of promised destruction Not very balanced weapons Conclusion: Overall, the game is very fun, and mostly brings what I was hoping for, outside of building destruction being lackluster compared to what was hoped for. I definitely recommend the game for anyone who can spare the cash or wait for a sale, as it’s a game that will keep you busy for a long time. Rating: 8.5/10 For full review head over to our website

review_text: I've been using Steam for 20+ years and to the best of my memory have never left a review. I'm just so sick of review bombing I feel the need to offset it. Review bombing a game because it's not COD or because you don't like Battle Royales, or whatever the case... Is wild behavior and bad for the industry. Something (which to my surprise) EA (or this specific team) is clearly trying to change back in the favor of the gamers themselves, at least in this brief window of time. If you have even the tiniest amount of logic you can see that BF6 being a massive success will only force COD and others to be good again, and listen to their community. I've played every battle royale essentially since the beginning, Dayz: Battle Royale / H1Z1 and tried everything since. To me, there was always something special with PUBG, and then COD Blackout took it to the next level, with Apex Legends bringing some new really nice mechanics (high risk reviving teammates, ziplines, great performance, etc). Warzone was an abysmal mistake coming off of Blackout. Impeccable timing lining up with the pandemic and everyone playing it while at home built a false narrative about the game to Activision, which ultimately lead to the comical trash heap it is today. Take the pandemic out and Blackout 2 comes out a year or so later to undo their mess. REDSEC is COD Blackout V2 with a spritz of Apex (given who's running the studio, no surprise), that is the best way to think about it. The perfect balance of simple mechanics with solid gunplay, no sprinting in circles dolphin diving around the map, no cash to farm to spam buy your loadout and revive your teammates 17 times straight... Most importantly, in the first 2 days I have experienced no game breaking bugs, we had a single crash across many hours of queues with 4 people, and the game is running at max settings, 4K 240 FPS locked 100% of the time without ever faltering. This alone should be praised (though it shouldn't have to be). Playing Warzone on 5090 at 4K has constant 1% drops, stutters, crashes, constantly recurring issues with the party and queuing system... Legitimately a terrible experience. Everyone knows these reviews are fake or just haters, ♥♥♥ it takes reading 20 of them to find one that actually references the gameplay. The first 10 I read were just simply mad there was a BR mode (just don't play it?) Keep it up EA, you are doing the right things, and the player counts show it. TLDR: If you like the high stakes open world feel of Battle Royales, this is arguably the best it's been done. It's hard to find anything significant to complain about. They clearly were very intentional in taking key aspects of the most popular BR games and blending them together. Never ending intense and comical moments, smooth movement, gunplay that feels like the better shot wins the fight, rock solid performance. Thumbs up.

review_text: I can accept getting destroyed by someone who’s genuinely better than me. Seriously. If a guy has better aim, better movement, better game sense—GG. That’s competition. What I can’t accept is losing to an invisible algorithm playing God behind the scenes. Same mouse. Same sensitivity. Same gun. Same shots. Yet somehow the bullets that were connecting perfectly yesterday are now passing straight through people like they’re made of smoke. Funny how that works. At some point, it stops feeling like you’re playing against other players and starts feeling like you’re playing against a spreadsheet that’s already decided who gets to win and who gets to lose. It’s like showing up to a boxing match only to discover the referee has secretly tied one of your arms behind your back because you’ve won too many rounds lately. And the best part? People will still tell you it’s a “skill issue.” Sure. My skill apparently dropped 40% overnight, recovered the next day, then disappeared again after a winning streak. What an amazing coincidence. So here’s my new strategy: if the game starts feeling weird within the first few matches—shots not registering, enemies becoming bulletproof, every fight feeling off—I’m not wasting my evening trying to convince an algorithm to let me play. I’ll just quit, play something else, touch grass, grab some food, and enjoy my life. The algorithm can queue up against itself.

SCW-10 (highest dps / best close range weapon) 3. SOR-300SC or AK-205 (SOR does more dps but AK has way better precision) 4. KTS100 (good bc of precision and range damage but nr 4 bc of 300-400ms scope in time compared to 160-200 for sl9 and low mobility) 5. KV9, USG-90, UMG (good early game smgs, replace them when you find something better from above) 666. Any sniper is good to have but i pref M210 or Mini Scout My fav loadout is SL9 + M210 or SCW-10+M210 Bugs to die for: Scout class proximity charge doesnt always show enemies which is just stupid. review_text: I rarely review games, but when I do, it's because something sticks with me so hard I can’t just shrug it off. RedSec’s Battle Royale is one of those cases. I love the idea of a Battlefield-style BR, but I hate how it’s executed here. Maybe it’s an unpopular opinion, but I have never understood why every Battle Royale insists on body armor that turns every fight into a two-mag dump just to kill one person. RedSec feels built for instant-dopamine, cracked-out CoD Warzone players. There is nothing about this mode that feels like Battlefield. It’s just Warzone with tanks and helicopters slapped on top. And why, why... are there automatic redeploys? If I wipe a squad, I shouldn’t have to kill them twice to make it stick. One death should be enough. Between the armor sponging and forced respawns, it completely ruins the pacing and meaning of winning gunfights. Final point: and this isn’t just RedSec, this is Battlefield in general, the netcode. How is it that after all these games, it’s still broken? I dream of the day I can peek a corner, take shots, give shots, and get back into cover without dying five seconds after I’m already behind a wall. Getting killed by bullets from the past isn’t “skill issue,” it’s just ♥♥♥ netcode.

review_text: Review: Battlefield RedSec (DLC) I was extremely disappointed with Battlefield RedSec. Battlefield 6 was an absolutely amazing game. I bought it at full price and never regretted it. It delivered exactly what I expect from a Battlefield title: large-scale battles, strong team play, and the classic zone capture gameplay that defines the franchise. However, RedSec feels completely out of place. The Battle Royale mode simply does not work in a Battlefield environment. It feels forced, unnecessary, and disconnected from what makes Battlefield great. The gameplay looks unpolished and uninspired, and overall it just doesn’t feel like Battlefield at all. Instead of trying to imitate games like Warzone, the developers should stick to their classic large-scale, objective-based warfare formula. That’s what Battlefield players love and expect. Honestly, I would rather start playing Warzone again than continue playing RedSec. This DLC does not live up to the Battlefield name and feels like a step in the wrong direction for the series.

review_text: I'm an avid MOBA fan, as with dragonball and when I heard that this game existed I really wanted to try and it play the game. Well I have now and I'm a bit split. On one hand the game is fun, the gameplay itself is fun it feels like a moba. however there are some very very prominent issues with this game. The MOBA Mechanics: They are very simple, 4 towers and the dragonball shell is all that exist in terms of a base. There no wards, but there is bushes and fog of war. There's no items just 3 perk cards which don't feel super impactful. There's a Helper system that also feels very unimpactful. in fact i forget to use them half the time and i still do well in fights The Characters and balance of said characters: The characters that are available are cool they are pretty accurate to their designs from the show the issue is some of these characters are wildly unbalanced. For example the newest addition Gogeta can ult for every fight after he gets it and it causes you to become executable at nearly half HP. {executes are instant death upon taking damage past a certain threshold) and he has a very annoying hard to dodge stun/knock up that nearly guarantees the the half HP execute every single time. This is an area effect as well so its not like you target one person and get get instantly executed you could do it to up to all 4 players on the enemy team even if that is unlikely. This is only the newest character there are a few others that are insanely overpowered. The biggest issues: Because of the lack of wards and the ability to have vision control the game very quickly falls a part and just becomes a race of who can backdoor the towers and dragonball shell first. 4v3 team fights are no longer a game winning fight its a game losing fight because that 1 person who isnt in that fight is just backdooring the towers. There's also a complete lack of minion waves and enemies can just do damage to your tower even if youre hitting them and canceling their gekishin bursts because even if they don't complete the charge up it still deals damage to the tower meaning you can just spam abilities on a low tower and it just dies there's no defending it as the defending team its just gone. There's times where i should have won a game and lost all because the enemy team constantly is able to just get free damage even though were clearly canceling their charges but because they have 2-3 people just spamming abilities dealing chip damage they can get through it no matter what. This game really has potential to be a great moba, they could remove the helper system and add wards, they could add actual minion waves instead of the very gimmicky zeno thing and it could be an actual good MOBA but as of right now the game is too simple and too easily abusable for actual MOBA players like myself to enjoy and the game is too complex and too hard for the average dragon ball fan to understand. With all of this being said i still oppose the overhaul they're planning. Turning this game into a marvel rivals/overwatch clone is just a disservice to the fans of this game and those who spent money on it. I wish i could give a mixed review because that's truly how i am on this game, on one hand its very fun and can be great with a full stack who knows what they're doing, but alone this game is a hellscape of people who don't fundamentally understand anything other than fighting the enemies.

review_text: Not Recommended (From Someone Who Actually Played the Game) I’ll just get this out of the way first so it’s clear this isn’t a “skill issue” review: I was S rank in every role. I’ve put in the time. I’ve seen the systems. I understand how this game works — which is exactly why I’m done with it. Let’s start at launch, where things immediately went great. By “great,” I mean persistent connection issues that lasted from release all the way through halfway into Season 1 (yes, the second ranked season). This wasn’t some mysterious edge-case bug — it was basic poor optimization and bad servers. A fantastic first impression for a competitive live-service game. Then there’s the monetization, which deserves a slow clap for sheer audacity. The game technically rewards premium currency... at a blistering pace of 10 gems per week, while a single new character costs 250 gems. Since launch — including events — I’ve earned 165 gems total. Incredible. At this rate, I might unlock a character sometime next decade. The star collection progression system somehow makes things even worse. Long-term players are actively punished for playing early. With recent changes, anyone who played since launch essentially overpaid for every hero they unlocked, by at least 250 gems’ worth. And that’s being generous, since this only accounts for the level 31 change that now allows unlocking Season 1 characters. Oh, and let’s not forget: it was originally intended that you would never be able to unlock newly released characters through star collection — only the previous season’s. This was only changed after backlash, not because it was a bad idea (it was), but because players noticed. Always a good sign. Hero leveling costs scale exponentially, while zeni — the standard non-premium currency — trickles in at a comically low rate. Translation: the longer you play, the harder progression becomes. For context, leveling from 1–109 costs the same as 109–119. That’s not balance — that’s a punishment loop. Balance-wise, new characters arrive feeling hilariously overtuned. SSJ4 Vegeta in particular feels like a panicked overcorrection to SSJ3 Goku, and it paints a very clear picture of how future releases will be handled. And wow, what a coincidence — Season 1 characters got nerfed right as Season 2 launched. Totally unrelated, I’m sure. What’s truly impressive is how every single season introduces new, innovative ways to make the game worse for F2P players and active players. Which is fascinating, because those are usually the people you want to keep in a live-service game. Bold strategy. As for gameplay: don’t expect creativity. This isn’t even as fun as Pokémon Unite. Scoring and backcapping barely matter. Towers barely matter as long as one is still standing. Deaths and XP feel irrelevant most of the time. The optimal strategy is to play defensively, avoid risks, and wait for objectives — because doing anything else is just asking to lose. It feels less like a MOBA and more like a diet League of Legends with fewer options and less agency. And before the Dragon Ball fans show up to explain that “they need to make money”: spare me. Literally every other successful F2P game figured this out years ago. Monetization does not have to come at the expense of fairness, progression, and player goodwill. The devs here didn’t just miss the memo — they ignored it entirely. Don’t play this. It’s greedy, restrictive, and steadily getting worse the more you engage with it. And that’s coming from someone who really, genuinely tried. -SR

review_text: So, as of recent news, this game will basically stop existing. They are replacing this game from a MOBA to a 3rd person hero shooter in the style of Marvel Rivals. This, masked as some big awesome news in lieu of the 1st anniversary of the game. This is the first time that I see a game completely morph into a whole different genre and gameplay style. And it certainly is the first time I see a game do that for it's first ever anniversary. It's as if you love your bicycle so to celebrate one year with it your parents decide to take it away and destroy it, giving you roller skates in return. Yeah, both are means of transportation, both can be fun, but maybe you simply prefer the bike, no? I think it would have been better to simply announce Gekishin Squadra would come to an end due to poor financial performance, and then announce a new game. I would perfectly understand if this title was simply a failure for Bandai and they needed to discontinue it. Now, who knows, maybe the new thing will be fun, but it certainly won't be anything like what we know today... By doing this, they're basically betraying the existing player base, which must be rather low considering that they have to resort to these tactics to rescue the game from the grave, then somehow they expect to get higher attention from new players in doing so. My prediction is that it will do the opposite, you will have the loyal player base gone, and with Marvel Rivals, Overwatch and even to this day Team Fortress 2 dominating the hero shooter genre, it will be impossible to compete with them unless they somehow make it such an extraordinary title that breaks the mold spectacularly. And it's just Bandai we're talking about in the end, so very unlikely. So, if you want to give it a try, do so before it's gone. Season 7 is officially the last season of this game as we know it, and after that it's gone forever. It's basically the requiem of what we had come to enjoy after a whole year of supporting the game. As always, this is just Bandai being one of the worst companies in existence. It's always been like so for games, figure lines, you name it. Absolutely scummy, predatory behavior through and through, zero regard for the customer, tunnel vision to simply return with as much cash as possible.

I am someone who played the game ever since it was first called Project: Multi, to this day I will stand by my opinion (fact) that it was a far superior experience compared to both Gekishin Squadra EM Test and full release. Fast forward one year later, infamous Game Director Toshi, the same one who ruined Dokkan Battle and Legends, decides Gekishin Squadra will be his next victim. So what have we got here? Removed content (Great Ape gone entirely), changed mechanics that actually made things worse (Gekishin Burst), pay-to-win characters and insanely questionable balance changes made for the sole purpose of forcing players into buying the latest shiny character that breaks the meta before they get nerfed to the ground (SSJ3 Goku became free for a week, immediately nerfed to the ground a week later lmao). Mind you, this is 6 MONTHS INTO THIS GAME'S LIFESPAN and THEY DECIDED IT WAS GOOD IDEA TO WHIPLASH EVERY OG PLAYER WHO GOT USED TO HOW THE GAME WORKED BY NOW. This was the last straw for me to simply quit this garbage and never look back. The last time I've seen news from Gekishin Squadra, it was community drama for the tournaments (lol) and a desperate attempt to appeal to the League of Legends pro players by organizing a livestream with them. I'm just going to say this: 1 minute of League of Legends Ranked is way more complex than an entire Gekishin Squadra tournament. There is no strategy involved, no team comp, no actual thought and professionalism put into these tournaments. This game is quite literally "pick busted characters, steal bosses unga bunga", a complete sad joke and anyone who believes they're "top" anything in this game are living in delusions of grandeur. Do yourself a favour, avoid this game like the plague and play something better like Heroes of the Storm.

review_text: Its a game that is still trying to find its feet. Its stumbled, it made mistakes. But I can definately say the devs are listening. For example: one of the biggest gripes I personally had, as a player, was the earning of zeni. Because it's required to star unlock. Which is required to unlock characters. And there was no easy way to earn zeni before. Now they default to giving you 1000 zeni every day you log in. Which is enough to star unlock a new character twice if you get enough of their shards (shards are given for playing that character.) This is to incentivize you to play new characters instead of just sticking to one or 2. They also added (a horrible but it exists) way to unlock characters every week by playing their role 10 times. Which leads to EVERYONE trying to play those roles and queue times go crazy as nobody wants to queue as any role except that specific role so they can unlock a free character. (This needs to change. Make it "play with the 'any' selection 10 times. Much healthier.) Gameplay If you ever played a MOBA, like Leauge of Legends or Dota 2, you will find things easy to adapt. There are no items, instead you get cards that you can choose from. Not a lot of selections, so its pretty easy to choose, and you can choose anywhere on the battlefield when you unlock one. Levels matter a LOT in this game. if you are 1 level below your enemy, prepare to know what it feels like to get the Yamcha treatment. If you are equal in level, it can come down to skill. If you are a level over them, you can greed for a kill. Tactics DOSE play a heavy role in this game, such as positioning and blind firing attacks into areas you THINK they might be to do surprise damage before they even know you exist. All in all, fun game 8/10. Fix that character unlocking system and It'll be 9/10. What's holding it back is that there is only a single map right now, and there is no incentive to play the other game modes as they give no rewards (last time I played them anyways.) Update: For those who just wanna have fun: you can play against the Intermediate AI and you will get the normal rewards (minus rank up of course). If you are on a lose streak and want a slightly challenging win: play against bots. Simple and clean fun. The AI is not super dumb, so it is still fun to steamroll them.

review_text: Gekishin squadra is a fantastic MOBA. The average playerbase is...less than fantastic, however. Much like any team oriented game, Toxicity is rampant, and the amount of overblown drama-farming is outright inane when it comes to character balance or the (Honestly, very tasteful) microtransactions present in the game (It is a free to play game after all.) I've played for 50 hours, and I've put a whole $20 into the game. I own every character, and pretty much every color for every character, along with many other cosmetics such as unique finisher moves, MVP screens, emotes, ect. And that $20 was more of an impatience thing than a "Getting something that you can't get for free" thing. I can admit, I am blessed to play with some of the funniest, coolest players, an entire full-stack team of amazing players who have hundreds more hours than I do, and play nightly, some even top 1000 worldwide players. (Keep in mind, this game doesn't exist only on steam.) This makes the play experience SO much cleaner, but I have spent time solo queue and I can absolutely admit that it's the same kind of hellish pain as playing league of legends, except no amount of ranking can save you from Elo hell. It's all Elo hell, because ranking is fairly easy with a decent team with competent players. I will use this moment to plug that I am actually writing a guide which will be showing up shortly in the Steam guides tab soon for the game with help from those same players, along with my decades (Yes, Decades. I'm old. I know.) of experience in MOBA's in general. The main things I LOVE about this game: • It's completely free to play, and P2W is nonexistent. No character ever launched has ever been so problematic that a little thinking, a little consideration, and a little learning of the matchups has been impossible to beat. Nothing is single-handedly winning people games. You can max out your entire account in no time, and many of the "meta" characters are part of your starting lineup. Also, the developers of the game CONSTANTLY pour free rewards down our throats. If you simply LOG IN AND DON'T EVEN PLAY you can get half of the characters in the game in like a week, and you get to choose what characters you get, and the more characters you have, the faster you level up. • The core gameplay of the game is simple to pick up, difficult to master. Generic statement I know, but it's true. The game simplifies a LOT of the mechanics from other MOBA games to the point. No mana mechanics mean abilities are flowing constantly. The depth comes from knowing how to synergize your abilities with your allies which adds a lot of options for teambuilding. No two teammates have an identical gameplan. • The characters are STUFFED with references. When you play Trunks, it feels like you're playing Trunks. When you play Buu, you feel like you're playing Buu. The moves, the voice lines, the synergies, the emotes and win-screens all OOZE with ...well...character! ANY character you can play, you can take one look at their ability list and your response will be "Yeah, that sounds about right". • The developers continue to constantly tweak, fix, and adjust the game to keep it fresh and interesting. Bosses change, events bring easy ways to earn rewards, and any rough patches since season 1 have been completely smoothed out, such as Getting enough Zenny to level, making it so that when you unlock all characters of a tier, you get a character of the next highest tier, and so on. • The way you unlock characters and the way progression works means the longer the game goes on, you get easier access to more characters. Characters go from "gems only" for a short time into Tier 1, then Tier 2, and Tier 3 and so on, Not only that, you get Gems for free weekly, so you can farm battle passes, you can farm gem costumes, I've even gone so far as to buy multiple battle passes for free, as well as a couple of characters all from just free gems and rotating battle pass rewards. The ONLY negative I can say about this game is the playerbase and the sloptubers who will call everything ever "Broken" before they even touch the game, and it results in an endless parade of clowns who will dive a tower and feed the enemy team because someone is playing a character they don't own, because in the minds of these people, if you own a character they don't own yet? It's OP. It's carrying you. If they finally get it? It's clearly nerfed into the ground because it isn't carrying them for free. That mentality is such a toxic waste dump and it's caused a lot of unwarranted negative reviews. People will post factually incorrect things such as "I can't unlock X character because there's not enough character unlock nodes on the progression tree" or "Gems improve your matchmaking odds" or nonsense like that. Please. Use your brains. Use common sense. REALLY look at the mechanics of the game. Because you know what? Despite everyone's complaints about new characters, when you ask the best players, the players who actually go out and win hundreds of games a week? They'll tell you the same things: Play with friends, Play who you like. Play using common sense. Play to your teams synergies. Be aware of the opponents synergies. And Surrendering is only reasonable when you have entirely AFK teammates who have full-send given up and are crashing out.

review_text: Just wanted to say... I really enjoy Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra, but the character unlock system is honestly a bit ridiculous. If you're already high level, it feels like there's no real way to get the new characters without spending gems... and you barely get 15 gems a week. That makes future updates feel kind of locked off unless you pay. On the other hand, I actually like that there's no chat. It avoids all the flaming, crying, and overreactions that ruin a lot of other games. People sometimes make "bold decisions" which can be good,but stuff like rushing into the God of Destruction zone before it’s even open by Zeno? Yeah, that’s trolling. And I don't think most players even realize the report button exists after a match. Use it. Hopefully they vanish from the queue. Trolls showing up even in A or S rank is rough, but the game is still fun. It’s like a Dragon Ball version of Dota, and I wish they added more cards or systems to customize builds - that’s something Dragon Ball usually shines at.

review_text: I was looking forward to the release of this game. Even though it wasn't playable for a while, I didn't overhype it or set my expectations too low; I was just waiting. I played it on both mobile and PC (using a different account), and my impressions are highly negative. 1) Terrible Optimization The optimization is awful. My phone gets incredibly hot only when playing this game; in any other game, it barely gets warm. Here, I literally have to use a phone cooler to keep the temperatures down. On PC, it gets moderately hot, which is still somewhat tolerable. 2) Awful Matchmaking The matchmaking takes forever and is poorly balanced. Even if you are Rank A, the game might pair you with Rank D players or literal beginners who have no idea what they are doing, leading to an instant loss. To make matters worse, you can get a bot on your team that constantly throws by running into enemy towers and dying, feeding the opponents and making them stronger. 3) Broken Balance Balance is the most crucial aspect of any MOBA, but here, every new character is completely overpowered compared to the rest. They dominate the meta for at least a month before getting nerfed. Furthermore, if you lose just one early-game fight, you are highly likely to lose the entire match. The enemy instantly gets a level advantage and stronger abilities, allowing them to freeze your lane and steal your farm. You can’t do anything about it, especially with a bot teammate constantly feeding. As for bosses and cards: once the enemy secures a boss, it gives them a massive advantage that is impossible to counter if you behind from the early game. Regarding the cards, honestly, only the damage-oriented ones are actually useful; the rest feel completely pointless. 4) Role Imbalance If you are playing solo, you are practically forced to play as an Attacker. Other roles are completely useless on their own. In a genre where teamwork is supposed to be key, this game simply rewards whoever deals the most damage. That’s all from me.

review_text: This is the biggest piece of garbage I've played so far, although the only other MOBA I've really played is Smite, so that's my point of comparison. The game is horribly unbalanced. Supports deal more damage than actual DPS characters, some DPS heroes can erase health bars in seconds, and tanks either die instantly or become literally immortal depending on some divine lottery. And that's not even mentioning the "divine lottery" items like the hammer, which encourage the most obnoxious hit-and-run playstyle imaginable. I've put around 90 hours into the game because some friends asked me to install it so I could join their premade team for a tournament. Since then, I've played both solo and with them, and I can confidently say that playing solo is one of the worst gaming experiences you can voluntarily subject yourself to. There are bots in ranked matches—actual bots. AFK players are everywhere. On top of that, there are bugs that can prevent you from spawning entirely or crash your game and stop you from reconnecting to the match. I genuinely can't recommend this game to anyone. I'm already bored of it, and I have a regular premade group, so I probably tolerate it more than most people would. But if you're looking to get into MOBAs, play something that's actually balanced and fun. Play Smite or League of Legends instead.

review_text: Not Recommended (Solo Queue Ranked) Gekishin Squadra has solid gameplay mechanics and can be genuinely fun... when matchmaking works. Unfortunately, that’s rare. Ranked solo queue is a mess. One match you’re teamed with competent players, the next you’re stuck with teammates who ignore objectives, don’t understand their roles, or rage after a single misplay. Meanwhile, the enemy team feels like a coordinated squad with perfect target focus and map awareness. Add in AFKers, ping spammers, and trolls who throw games over petty drama, and it becomes a frustrating grind. The reward system doesn’t justify the effort, making it hard to stay motivated. To make matters worse, pay-to-win mechanics are deeply embedded. Sure, you can grind gems to unlock characters, but the process is painfully slow and time-gated. Events that award gems are limited, and realistically, you can expect to unlock a new Z-tier character maybe once a year as a free-to-play player. Meanwhile, premium characters like SSJ3 Goku are blatantly overpowered, dominating the meta and making competitive progression feel hopeless unless you pay up. Until proper matchmaking is implemented, solo queue toxicity is addressed, and the monetization model is rebalanced, I can’t recommend this game in good faith.

review_text: MOBAs can be frustrating because a player must have a competent group of players on their team in order to succeed. What makes a game even more frustrating is when the designers aren't even trying to give consideration to how more serious players, who aren't simply fans of a franchise, engage with the game. The game mechanics, screen popups that obscure half of the battlefield, loose controls, buggy skill firing, mobile interface on a PC game... there are many issues that prevent this game from being playable, long-term, for any serious gamer who has played games for decades. There is also no way to communicate to players on what they might be doing wrong aside from by far the worst and most annoying "ping" visuals and sounds ever created. The game is fun, the art style and some of the mechanics are really good. Others are so bad that it takes away from the good to the point where after a severe loss against Pay to Win heroes like Gotenks and SSJ3 Goku, or due to having what appear to be bots on the team, a player like myself will move on. This is another example of the art and style dominating a game, and the developers dropping the ball when it comes to gameplay. This is a mobile game ported to PC. If this were a real Dragon Ball Z MOBA for PC, that would be rad. It could be that, but the publisher doesn't want to create that apparently.

O jogo é de GRAÇA, é óbvio que vão ter maneiras deles farmarem um dinheirinho, mas no caso deste jogo, nem é algo grave, pelo amor de Deus. Eu joguei Pokemon Unite, joguei por 2 meses e só tinha comprado uns 3 ou 4 bonecos, eu joguei isso aqui por 5 horas e já tenho 5 bonecos, 5 BONECOS. As pessoas tem que maneirar um pouco nessas críticas, poxa, não gostou do jogo ser assim? Então vai pro Click Jogos, bicho. Os caras com 40 horas reclamando disso, 30 horas falando essas besteiras... Padre/Pastor, é pecado jogar Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra? Que nada, é muito é massa!! Porém, o maior problema deste jogo são os constantes crash e erros de conexão. Eu já passei por vários crash apenas por clicar em 1 boneco no menu, ou dentro da partida, ou fazendo NADA KKK Olha, isso é total padrão Bandai, ainda mais em relação a instabilidade dos servidores, odeio bastante a Bandai por conta de nunca resolver esses problemas ou demorar muito para que finalmente se resolva. Ela espera o jogo morrer do que consertar essas coisas :( Se o jogo não tive tantos crash e os problemas de conexão "Esses que te desconectam direto da partida", eu daria nota 10/10, como tem esses problemas, vou ter que dar um 9.9 Que foi? É Dragon Ball, gente, brasileiro ama Dragon Ball, tem que dar avaliação boa, fez a infâncias de todos nós e o jogo ainda é do caramba, lindo, roda suave (Em quesito de fps). É um sonho esse jogo, muito bom mesmo, recomendo demais para quem é fã do anime/mangá. Edit: Cheguei no negócio de estrela level 12, escolhi pegar o Cooler, fui ver o boneco para ver se eu tinha uma skin. Cliquei duas vezes nele e o jogo crashou. SIMBORA, FAMÍLIA, CONTINUAREI JOGANDO MESMO ASSIM PQ O JOGO É MUITO É MASSA! Edit 07/11/2025: Eles tem limitação para ganhar os fragmentos dos personagens, uma limitação que é determinada pela quantidade de partidas que você vai jogar em 1 dia. Fiquei triste, mas ao menos não é uma limitação de UMA SEMANA igual o Pokemon Unite. Eu gostaria mil vezes mais desse game se ele não tivesse essa limitação que é muito comum em jogos mobile. Continua sendo um jogasso, mas acho que seria muito mais interessante se ao menos eu pudesse continuar adquirindo esses shards jogando alguma especie de "Modo História" dos bonecos, ou se tivesse missões que dessem um número X de fragmentos para o boneco que você selecionasse, fiquei triste, mas continuarei jogando, pois estou apenas a duas casas para pegar o Cell. Engraçado que mesmo com essa limitação, continuei jogando muito o game, e continuaria ainda mais se o limite de fragmentos não fosse tão baixo "Estou pegando apenas 3 fragmentos jogando com qualquer boneco". O jogo está incrível, sou muito fã do Honor of Kings e do Pokemon Unite, se eu pudesse fazer o meu top tier de mobas, com certeza seria algo do tipo: 1 - DBZ: Gekishin Squadra, 2 - Honor of Kings, 3 - Pokemon Unite. Não joguem League of Legends, é horrível, verdadeiramente péssimo. Joguei do inicio de 2021 ao inicio de 2024, nunca havia tocado nesses mobas do mobile, são infinitamente melhores, mais divertidos, obviamente mais rápidos e etc. Recomendo demais jogar os mobas de celular, são maravilhosos, esse DBZ está sensacional, com todos os problemas de crash e etc. Eu amei e indico super para quem gosta do gênero moba. Não sei se eles estavam jogando em outras plataformas além do pc, mas sendo sincero aqui, todos os personagens que joguei até o momento são muitissimo bem balanceados, surpreendentemente, todos entram nessa casa dos que conseguiria levar uma partida no bolso só por usar 1% da minha capacidade cerebral. Gente, preste muita atenção nos boss do game e principalmente: OLHEM O MAPA!!! Sempre vai haver um espertinho querendo pontuar de graça, sejam cavalheiros e defendam a sua base pessoal. Eu peguei um monte de free kill por conta disso KASKDKASDKSADASKASKD Além de ajudar os seus amigos nas outras lanes, mesmo sendo early game. Galera, pensa comigo, se não tem boss na sua lane, o senhor zeno está na lane dos caras, mas você não consegue passar por eles, bicho, só vai na lane de cima e ajuda a defender ou PEGA O BOSS QUE ESTIVER LÁ! review_text: P2W slop. For everyone wondering why your teammates are so dumb or why every match is just a one sided blow-out for one team, it's because the game purposefully matches you with bots. Sometimes you get the bots on your team and sometimes you get bots on the other team. The game clearly has EOMM (Engagement Optimized Matchmaking) and these bots are their poor way of implementing it. The bots have existed since the playtests and continue to plague nearly every single match. We know that there were bots in the playtests not just by the obvious bot way they were playing, but because they all had names of the NPC characters from the 3DS game Dragon Ball Fusions, made by the same developers of Gekishin Squadra. As far as I'm aware they've stopped doing this naming convention in the official release to try and make it less obvious that you're playing with bots. I am S rank (the highest rank you can achieve in the game) in the Technical role and the bot problem never went away, even at the highest rank in the game. Here are just some of the ways you can tell you are playing in a bot match: - Teammates cycle through characters extremely fast in the selection screen, and all of them get ready shortly after you do - They never pick a preferred lane - They pick the most random helpers. If you see both your dps pick metallic despite no buns, or your tank pick Icarus, get suspicious - Whenever Zeno is arriving at the enemy tower, one of the bots will consistently ping that tower, exactly once - Bots have bizarre pathing towards the lane at the beginning of the game - If you are going top, the bot will go too far up and then have to go back down again at the first minion, instead of going to it in a straight line - If you are going bottom, if you kill the minions before the cell jrs spawn, the bot will suddenly attempt to go top, presumably because there are no objectives to go to in bot lane, then suddenly turn around when the cell jrs spawn

review_text: A wonderful celebration of the Rusty Lake series and the folks behind it. I must say this game took me on a surprise rollercoaster, transforming from another Rusty Lake title to a package of easter eggs and details nodding to previous titles, as well as other game the Dev team has worked on outside of this series. I was taken by surprise when the game transformed beyond the magic show into your character helping to continue 'developing' the game, within a game. My favorite details were in the office where you could take a look at various artifacts from the Rusty Lake series, both mainly on the shelves and scattered around the room. My personal favorite is the in-game photos on the phone of the Dev team, it's a personal favorite of mine when you get to see the team behind something within a title. I also love the attention to detail when the player interacts with the phone being able to break the 4th wall. Overall, the length of the puzzles and their difficulty were just right. Although I did find the knife puzzle a bit trivial, the rest of the puzzles were very intuitive and followed a similar pattern known if you have played any previous titles. The Dev team and their Rusty Lake series will always hold a special place in my gaming history as one of the first titles that captivated mean back on flash alongside the Henry Stickman series and a Small Favor series.

review_text: I think it is one of the best puzzle games I have ever played, and I would highly recommend it. The game drops you into a mysterious magic performance filled with hidden secrets, where you sit in the audience and watch Mr. Rabbit perform on a small stage. While the show unfolds, you will constantly interact with the stage as you play, clicking on the magic hat, opening curtains, and exploring different props. Every small action can trigger something unexpected, which makes it feel like the performance is alive and reacting to you. What I really like is how the game keeps making me question what is real and what is just part of the trick. Each act feels like a short puzzle, but there are almost no direct instructions, so you are always observing carefully and trying things out on your own. The atmosphere is also very unique. It starts off cozy and playful, almost like a charming little magic show, but slowly it begins to build layers of mystery and a subtle sense of unease.
