review_text: A Worthy Successor to Battlefield 4 and Battlefield V Recommended 👍 After playing Battlefield 4 and Battlefield V, Battlefield 6 is the next Battlefield game that has really caught my attention. The gunplay feels great, the shooting mechanics are satisfying, and the overall gameplay has that Battlefield feel that makes the series so enjoyable. The graphics are pretty nice too, and the visuals help make the battles feel immersive. The gunplay is definitely one of the biggest highlights for me. Weapons feel good to use, and getting into firefights is genuinely fun. Coming from Battlefield 4 and Battlefield V, I'm happy with what Battlefield 6 brings to the table. It feels like a solid addition to the franchise, and I've been enjoying my time with it. My only major complaint so far is the matchmaking. Finding a match can take longer than it should, which gets frustrating when all you want to do is jump into the action. Hopefully, this gets improved in future updates. Overall, I'm having a great time with Battlefield 6. The gunplay is excellent, the graphics look good, and the core Battlefield experience is enjoyable. Fix the matchmaking issues, and this could be an even better experience. Verdict: Recommended. If you're a Battlefield fan, especially if you've enjoyed BF4 and BFV, Battlefield 6 is worth checking out. See you on the battlefield! 🎮

review_text: Battlefield 6 abandons everything that made this franchise great and desperately chases Call of Duty's style until it breaks. The fast pacing is completely overdone, and the mandatory slide mechanics make every encounter feel cheap and unstrategic. Gunfights aren't won by positioning or tactics anymore because everybody can be heard like they're an elephant. The marketing and "cool" aesthetic can’t hide the fact that the core gameplay lacks FUN and identity. There’s no weight to the shooting, no satisfaction in conquering a map together, and no room for the chaotic, unpredictable moments that made old Battlefield legendary. It’s clear where DICE’s priorities lie: engagement metrics and wallet extraction over player experience.

review_text: The modern version of a classic bait and switch. The beta was legitimately the best part of this game because, at the time, I assumed the full release would be more fleshed out. Boy was I wrong. Battlefield 6 is a game that keeps showing you it could have been a real Battlefield, then immediately reminds you it chose to be something else. The gunplay is ok enough to hook you for a few matches, and there are moments where the action feels like classic Battlefield. Those moments are so rare they feel almost accidental. A lot of it comes down to flow. Good Battlefield maps give you options. You can push the objective straight on, flank, take a side route, go up a neighboring building, or use vehicles to create pressure somewhere else. In BF6, you get funneled into the same two or three choke points, and once one team gets control, you might as well wait for the next objective. As a side note, I’m not sure who decided which maps get what vehicles and when, but that person should at least be given a stern talking to. Maps are trash. First off, they are tiny. The playable area alone limits options. Most maps only have a handful of lanes or are extremely flat and open. City maps are filled with locked doors and hallways that lead nowhere. Objective locations for game modes were not planned out well, and in combination with small maps and limited lanes, some rounds are not even worth playing. For comparison: BF6 launch maps average: 0.189 km2 (9 maps) BF4 launch maps average: 0.784 km2 (8 maps I could find sizes for) So BF4’s launch maps are about 4.15x larger. TTK is trash too. It plays like COD so they could appeal to a larger player base. For comparison: In Battlefield 4, most assault rifles used the standard 24.5 max damage model, which means 5 point blank body shots to kill a 100 HP player. So the math looks like this (stock, point blank, body shots): AEK 971 (900 RPM, 5 shots to kill) TTK = (shots to kill − 1) × (60 ÷ RPM) TTK = (5 − 1) × (60 ÷ 900) = 4 × 0.0667 = 0.267s (267ms) M416 (750 RPM, 5 shots to kill) TTK = (5 − 1) × (60 ÷ 750) = 4 × 0.0800 = 0.320s (320ms) ACE 23 (770 RPM, 5 shots to kill) TTK = (5 − 1) × (60 ÷ 770) = 4 × 0.0779 = 0.312s (312ms) Now compare that to Battlefield 6. DougS2K’s BF6 Weapon Stats Spreadsheet (posted on the Battlefield 6 subreddit and hosted on Google Sheets) has point blank body TTKs like: TR 7: 0.167s (167ms) M4A1: 0.200s (200ms) B36A4: 0.250s (250ms) M433: 0.217s (217ms) So in BF4, typical AR gunfights are around the 312 to 320ms zone. In BF6, it can be as low as 167ms. It may not seem like much, but in game it is extremely noticeable, especially if you are a veteran Battlefield player. Weapons... Not even sure where to start here. I will just say that the weapons seem to contradict how the intended class playstyle is supposed to go down. The whole point of classes is tradeoffs. You pick a role, you bring certain strengths, you accept certain weaknesses, and your team makes up the difference. That is the Battlefield multiplayer identity. BF6 does not respect that. Everyone can build into everything, so class identity gets watered down into basically nothing. Some more comparisons: BF4: 80+ launch weapons BF6: 45 unlockable weapons BF6 (extra): +12 weapons via assignments after Career Rank 50 How long to unlock each weapon (worst case, last rank gated unlock): BF4: Rank 60 total = 3,520,000 XP 25,000 XP/hr: 3,520,000 / 25,000 = 141 hrs 40,000 XP/hr: 3,520,000 / 40,000 = 88 hrs 60,000 XP/hr: 3,520,000 / 60,000 = 59 hrs BF6: Career Rank 2 to 50 unlock track About 72 hrs to hit Rank 50 and unlock all Career weapons (not counting the extra 12) How long to unlock all attachments per weapon? BF4 (kills based): 400 to 500 kills to “finish” a gun 40 KPH: 400 to 500 / 40 = 10.0 to 12.5 hrs 60 KPH: 400 to 500 / 60 = 6.7 to 8.3 hrs 90 KPH: 400 to 500 / 90 = 4.4 to 5.6 hrs BF6 (mastery): Mastery 50, about 1,800 kills per gun 40 KPH: 1,800 / 40 = 45 hrs 60 KPH: 1,800 / 60 = 30 hrs 90 KPH: 1,800 / 90 = 20 hrs Finally, Vehicles... They can be fun for a bit, but nothing like previous installments. Map size and cover really limit options. Variety is also extremely limited. For comparison: BF4: ~50 vehicles at launch BF6: 15 vehicles Makes sense considering the size constraints the BF6 maps introduce. Vehicles seem like they may have been an afterthought, with no map specifically built around vehicle use. Unfortunately, this is probably as close to classic Battlefield as EA is going to give us these days. Buy it if you want to scratch the BF itch. It will not be satisfying, but it is all you are going to get. review_text: Once again, despite having a clear blueprint for making one of the best FPS franchises in gaming, the developers have delivered a half-baked, uninspired product. The game feels stagnant, underdeveloped, and eerily reminiscent of Battlefield 2042. In trying to appeal to everyone, it ends up appealing to no one. The identity crisis is obvious. The game attempts to cater to Call of Duty–style players with faster movement and pacing, yet CoD players don’t want Battlefield—they already have CoD, and they quickly go back to it. Meanwhile, long-time Battlefield fans are alienated from the start. The slower, immersive experience of BF3, BF4, and BF1—defined by weighty gunplay, powerful sound design, large-scale immersion, and meaningful destruction—is largely gone. Instead of doubling down on what made Battlefield unique, the developers once again chose microtransactions and flashy skins that feel completely out of place. These cosmetics add nothing to the experience and only further erode the franchise’s identity. What truly set Battlefield apart from its competitors—Levolution—has been stripped down to the bare minimum. Watching a crane fall is dull compared to entire buildings collapsing in BF4. Minor environmental damage doesn’t come close to the widespread, dynamic destruction seen throughout BF1, or the unforgettable cinematic moments like the zeppelin crashing mid-match. Map design only amplifies the problem. Air vehicles are placed into maps so small and restrictive that a single dogfight can push you out of bounds nine times out of ten. The scale feels wrong, the flow feels broken, and the chaos that once defined Battlefield is missing. From the moment the game reused the BF2042 engine, expectations were already low. While it may be an improvement over that disastrous release, it still falls far short of earning the Battlefield name. At best, it’s a slightly more polished version of a failed direction—proof that the franchise still hasn’t learned from its mistakes. I appreciate those who have something to say, be it positive or negative, but please, for your own sake, do not label a review as “made with ChatGPT” just because you saw someone use the infamous em dash to emphasize a point. The em dash is not an AI invention, nor is it a giveaway of AI writing. It has been used by writers long before AI became common, because it helps show a pause, a shift in thought, or emphasis in a way that commas and periods sometimes do not. This is my opinion, and only my opinion. If you enjoy the game, play it as much as you want. But as someone who dislikes the path game development is taking, and even more, the degradation of a franchise I cherish so much, I took it upon myself to put into words what I felt. When I read reviews from those who play a game and review it, it gives me an idea of either the state of the game or the bias around it. Money might be unimportant to some, but to those who appreciate the opinions of others before spending theirs, here lies mine.

review_text: Battlefield 6 is not a Battlefield game for Battlefield veterans. That, at its core, is fine. If Battlefield Studios want to cater to a different market, there is no problem with that. That said, as a long time franchise veteran, with thousands of hours across Bad Company 2, BF3, BF4, BF1, and BFV... I'm just tired, man. There are other reviews with walls of gripe about this game and those of them that mention previous experience with the franchise will all say the same thing: "this game isn't for us any more." The most glaring evidence of this is the removal of class-locked weapons, and even class-locked playlists. Gone, in pursuit of something very, very different. The maps are too crowded, too small, or too directionless. Remade maps have been shrunk, or changed to fit one particular playstyle; run and gun. A particular gripe of mine is how redundant snipers feel now. Never mind that every single sniper that has been added to the game is worse than the starting one, never mind that there is an attachment that literally zeroes the scope for you, removing half of the fun of figuring out hold points, never mind that an M4 with a couple of attachments will burst you down over 500+m quicker than you can rechamber a round if you miss your headshot... nobody even bothers. I see no snipers in this game, and when I do, they're running a rangefinder. It's boring. The remakes of Golmud and Firestorm? Boring. The small town at the top of Golmud, which was once a main thoroughfare that could be reliably held by a few well-placed engineers? Now a sprawling close-quarters arena, with too many angles to make defence a reliable option. Just let it get taken and attack again. All of the verticality, rocks that snipers could sit on? Flattened. There's one now, at the back of the map, obstructed by the same town with no view onto other objectives. Firestorm has been shrunk, and the petroleum containers on the right side of the map which once provided a little verticality are now destructible - all but guaranteeing that if you kill someone from there, they'll just get in a tank and blow it up so you can't use it. This game makes me physically tired to play. I'm not young. I don't particularly want to engage with the fast-paced, "sprint around like a headless chicken" form of play that this game all but incentivises. I never did in previous games, why would I want to now? Why are you giving me no other viable option? Look, if you like fast-paced close-quarters gameplay, then I'm sure this game is perfect for you, and I would encourage you to play it, to enjoy it. But for me, and so many others, who never sought that experience in Battlefield and knew that our playstyle was just as viable in all other entries to the franchise, even 2042 for goodness sakes... it's just not there, and it's clear that Battlefield Studios only intend to move further and further away from what this franchise used to be. What a disappointment. What a tremendous, saddening disappointment. --- Just to add a little amendment to the bottom here, as a lot of people have brought it up. I have played every battlefield game, that includes 1942 and even 2142, I just didn't play for hours upon hours with those games, at least not to the same extent that I did with the games I actually mentioned above. There's a lot of ♥♥♥ measuring going on in the comments about whether I'm a "true battlefield veteran," it's not that deep guys. I've been here from day 1, and love the older games, I just didn't grow up on them like I did the others so didn't mention them.

review_text: It really is a shame what was once my favourite game series has turned into. In the beta and at launch Battlefield 6 actually seemed decent and I was optimistic they may have finally figured out how to make a good Battlefield again and while there are improvements over 2042 it is sadly still not enough. I was expecting to put 1000+ hours into this game as I have with most other Battlefields but after just nearly 300 hours I had to admit myself it just isn't fun at all. The netcode wasn't great at the start but somehow it has just gotten worse as time goes on. You can immediately tell if the netcode is ''on your side'' after your first gunfight in a match and sadly it is nearly always against you. Not that having it on your side really makes it any better as you can still clearly feel the unfairness. You can accept dying in what feels like one hit and having 0 time to react or dying when you are meters behind cover already if it just happens every now and then but it is nearly every game and has only become more unbearable since launch. One of the most important things in an online fps such as this is that it at least feels fair but this game just doesn't. The matchmaking is completely broken. Although they have never confirmed it my friends and I strongly suspect there is some sort of skill based matchmaking being used and I do believe this is why they refuse to add a server browser for official servers. Really what is the reason to not have a server browser other than if you want to force players into your matchmaking system? This again ties into the game just feeling unfair. I'm not the best player in the world but i'm no means the worst and have no problems getting into the top 5 of the scoreboard in a match but any sort of skill doesn't seem to matter when 95% of your matches are completely stacked against you. Sure you get the odd match where you're on the team that completely steamrolls the other but again there is no fun in that at all. The worst part is the extremely rare times you do get a match that is somewhat balanced and the netcode is okay the game is actually fun to play but this makes it all the more frustrating. There is a good game underneath all that but their stubbornness and inability to fix things means you rarely get to experience that. The content updates are also extremely disappointing. While I understand Battlefield is now a live service game 2 maps a season (that don't even release together) with 2 or 3 new guns is simply not enough and when they do things like release the little bird in season 2 it is blatantly obvious they are just holding things back to pad out seasons rather than making extra actual content. The battlepass is mostly filler too, what the game lacks in new maps and weapons there is no shortage of cosmetics and ''limited time modes'' which I guess is great if you're into that but most people aren't. I don't know a single person who would rather have another limited time mode that will be forgotten in a week over another map. The game already has the main Battlefield modes people buy it for with conquest, breakthrough, rush and a few smaller modes like TDM. Why do they insist on adding these things no one asks for? Portal seemed like it could be good until they yet again completely nerfed it immediately after launch. Personally i'm not someone who enjoys leaving my PC on in a portal server for hours to unlock everything but at the same time I really don't care if other people do. The game has 5000 ranks and while it doesn't seem fun if people want to just unlock all their weapons without actually engaging in pvp who cares? But the real downside to nerfing the xp in portal isn't that people can't boost its that it just automatically guarantees no one will use it. There has been some very interesting modes and maps people have created in portal that are completely dead because the simple fact is people still want to earn xp for playing and you can't do that if your server has any bots in it. They have also outright removed player created maps from other games (i.e shipment from call of duty). They provided a decent map editor that will just go to waste now. Why not have a monthly community vote or something on player created maps and add them into some sort of rotation or even turn them into actual maps? I saw several maps created from the California update alone that are all now completely dead. People are literally doing your job for you creating new maps and experiences but again they just seem to refuse to capitalise on any of it and it is so frustrating. I could go on but I think that gives you a good idea of where Battlefield is now. It used to be an amazing series that would take up nearly all of my time but the thought of playing it anymore is just tiring. The game will continue to haemorrhage players if they continue in this direction and sadly I don't see it changing. Look how many people have gone back to older Battlefield titles these past few days since they went on sale, you have the formula right there on how to make a Battlefield people want DICE so why do you refuse to do it?

review_text: You know how a game being almost good is in a sense way worse than it just actually being bad? Yeah that's Battlefield 6. I can't remember the last time I have been this pissed of at a game I actually kind of like. It's not quite bad enough to just walk away and it's infuriating beyond belief. Especially because it's unnecessarily bad in some places and it would have been so easy to just not screw it up. Or at least not screw it up as bad. At it's core it's almost a return to form the franchise desperately needed. HOWEVER! Apart from the core BF experience it commits almost every single mortal sin of live service nonsense like going down a checklist: Battlepass? ✓ check! Time limited fomo mini Battlepass in the bigger Battlepass? ✓ double check Regular ads for the battlepass you have to dismiss before even reaching the main menu? ✓ hold to check! Additional cosmetic store? ✓ you bet! Free to play Battle Royale glued to my 70€ shooter? ✓ CHEEECK! Challenges for said battle royale gunking up my weekly challenges? ✓ hell yeah! I do not have the BR installed and still get challenges for it which is just baffling - Does this go both ways? Do BR players get Challenges for a Multiplayer they did'nt buy? I don't even know which answer to this would make me more mad. And even after this, the single most annoying thing the bugs - not little bugs and glitches (haha look! my screen looks funny, when my sqadmate uses his recon gadgets) No, it's the ones that really take away from the experience and the devs apparently can't be asked to fix in a timely manner. At release peoble were abusing a drone glitch to get to inaccessible roofs. These were in almost every lobby FOR. SIX. WEEKS. And then they somehow managed to break the defibrilators for support, about 3-4 weeks ago. It's still broken! I am pretty sure this was in the same patch the other one was fixed, putting the time of this game functioning without issue at a whopping 0 days since release. Plus some minor things like no persistent lobbies, the awful smart TV interface and just how godawful some maps are. The only reason new Sobek is not the worst map in the entire franchise is because they released Blackwell Fields. Amazing! Unless you are a hardcore Battlefield fan or your friends are and they want to play with you, don't bother. Not for 70 Bucks at least. Now if you'll excuse me, I need to finish my procedurally generated weekly challenges for the battlepass!

review_text: I was willing to put up with so much because the game itself is fun, and the devs seem to be actually fixing the stuff that is broken and trying to make things better. This is ridiculous though. I can't recommend buying this. If you could get in for free, it would be worth playing. But it really feels like I paid $70 for a free to play game. It's not Battlefield 4. Cool, didn't think it would be. It would be naive to think that we could just have a new game that is like older games, but at least it's fun for what it is. Small, janky maps, odd class decisions. At least the guns feel good. Launch at $70, sure whatever, money isn't what it used to be. Premium $100 version. I thought it was just cosmetic, but actually, the thing that looks like just cosmetic skins, the "weapon packages" come with a suite of attachments already on them, which is meaningful before anyone's had time to grind out the levels on those weapons to legitimately unlock them. They also function as attachment loadouts. This is probably why they nerfed grinding bots for weapon attachments and won't let us do it in single player. More "cosmetic" purchases in the shop. Looks like standard games industry slop, but it's just cosmetic, right? There's the aforementioned "weapon packages," as well as character skins. What's wrong with character skins? Well, you can equip them on any class, so your enemy can't easily tell at a glance what class you are. Normally, if someone is a recon, you can tell by the ghillie shoulders. Not if they have one of these paid skins on. Battle pass. I get it, every "games as a service" model AAA game has this now. It's just cosme- wait, no it's not. There's weapons in here. What the heck? Well, at least you can just unlock them after a while just playing normally. Okay, whatever. I'll deal with it. Today, they released an update with a new map, a new gun, and new cosmetics (of course, but whatever.) Awesome. Love to see some new variety. Let's use the new gun. Oh it's locked, how do I unlock it? ... A limited time "Bonus" battle pass path that only lasts for 3 weeks. They locked the new weapon in a temporary battle pass, so you have to play consistently over the next 3 weeks (or pay $16.50) in order to unlock it. I don't want to overstate it. Life goes on, right? I probably won't even be playing this game in a couple months. However, man, it feels bad. It feels cheap. This is the kind of thing I expect from a free to play game. It really does feel like I paid $70 for a f2p game. So, as much as I enjoyed playing this game, and as much as I will continue to play it, I really can't recommend it to a prospective buyer.

review_text: BF6 is like a pretty ex-girlfriend who managed to claw her way back into your life, only to disappoint you again. All the promotional content for the game is very situational and specifically captured and shown off to give you the best impression. A lot of what is showcased is not often experienced while playing a match. Why does Bad Company 2 have better destruction and physics? Why does Battlefield 4 have very comparable graphical fidelity and only to use 3 GB of VRAM on max settings at 4K? Vehicles in BF6 are so imbalanced compared to previous games, and it never gets addressed in patch notes. How many seasons do you guys need? I’m tired of logging in only to be greeted with “Buy Battlefield Pro,” “Get the Battle Pass,” and guns locked behind a paywall. I already purchased the game, EA. I feel like people are starting to forget how good the old Battlefield games were and are blindly opening their wallets to be part of the latest entry. review_text: Battlefield 6 – A Disappointing Decline After a Promising Start I genuinely enjoyed the BETA. It felt fresh, chaotic in a good way, and full of potential. But now, as the full game unfolds, Battlefield 6 is slowly sliding downhill, and the issues are becoming too big to ignore. A Campaign That Feels Like a Tutorial The campaign is simply bad. There’s no weight, no excitement, and no Battlefield identity. It plays like an extended tutorial designed to funnel you into multiplayer, not a real single-player experience worth buying the game for. New Game Modes Bring Nothing Meaningful Modes like Sabotage sound interesting on paper, but in reality they add nothing valuable. Most of these new modes take place on tiny slices of maps where 16v16 players run around in kamikaze-style chaos, spamming RPGs at objectives that give less XP than actual combat. It’s messy, shallow, and completely disconnected from the classic Battlefield experience. Challenges Are Not “Challenges” The challenge system is one of the most frustrating parts of the game. Challenges don’t push players to try cool strategies or master their class, they simply force you into game modes you don’t want to play, like Battle Royale or Sabotage, just to check boxes and fill bars. Why should a long-time Battlefield player who enjoys Conquest, Breakthrough, or Rush be required to grind a free Battle Royale mode to unlock gear? Spending hours in a mode you don’t enjoy isn’t rewarding, it just creates burnout and resentment. Spawn Issues and Small-Map Chaos Many new modes take place on tiny map cuts, creating constant spawn traps and unavoidable deaths. It’s a run-die-repeat loop that feels more like an arcade shooter than a large-scale tactical FPS. Infantry Gameplay Has Lost the Battlefield Identity I prefer infantry gameplay, teamwork, class synergy, tactical pacing. Battlefield 6 instead leans into constant, frantic run-and-gun action. Playing Medic or Engineer feels unrewarding. I end up picking Assault just to survive the chaos. The Game Is Drifting Toward Call of Duty I never wanted to compare Battlefield to Call of Duty. In fact, I always hated when people said “BF is becoming CoD.” But after today’s session... I’m starting to see it. This constant run-and-gun chaos, the tiny arenas, the instant deaths from five directions the moment I spawn, it all feels less and less like Battlefield and more like Call of Duty with every update. And that’s worrying. For the first time in over a decade of playing this franchise, I actually found myself swearing at the screen and getting angry. That’s not healthy, and it’s not the Battlefield experience I’ve known. Dying to a heli is normal, that’s Battlefield. But getting deleted instantly on spawn, unable even to see the enemy, feels awful and cheap. Conclusion Battlefield 6 had potential, and the BETA looked promising. But the current direction feels completely disconnected from what made Battlefield special. Forced challenges, shallow game modes, spawn frustration, and a shift toward fast arcade-style gameplay all erode the Battlefield identity. Right now, it feels like the developers are chasing Call of Duty instead of doubling down on what their own fanbase wants. If the game doesn’t course-correct soon, it risks losing the very community that kept the franchise alive for decades.

The Verdict Stop giving this company a pass. They sold us another half-baked tech demo disguised as a full-price shooter. review_text: You know I was going to put a fairly positive review had they not made some really stupid decisions with the updates on this game. Apparently you can go to level 5000 in this game, this is something that should carry over in future BF games if you all remember how to make them that is, sadly I don't think the game will have the longevity for anyone to accomplish this legitimately. Some context to credentials for anyone who cares. I have 810,775 infantry kills over 2 accounts (not counting any vehicles) on BF1. I have always primarily played Conquest with the exception of Rush on BC2 and have been playing BF since 2005 starting with BF2. So I have played BF2, BF3, BC2, BC2 Vietnam, BF4, BF1, BFV, 2042 and BF6. Also have around 16k+ hours of time on CS, I was playing way before steam logged playtime, with the most of those hours being on CS:S and CS:GO. I'm not going to include everything wrong with this game but I would like to touch on some points. Squad size of 4 is a joke. Long term BF players have long grown used to 5 player squads. 5 works better in every scenario and makes more sense and gives squads more options than 4 players can achieve. You all stated you made this change so someone didn't get left out of a squad because of 64 player servers. Guess what has always happened with previous BF games? Some people don't join a squad at all and some people prefer to play that way (I personally want to always be in a full squad). So who were you punishing with 4 player squads? This changes the entire dynamic of BF. Players that have played together for years feel left out and alone because they can't join friends in a squad because it was changed to 4 players. So they get stuck in undesirable squads that have no coordination and no common sense. BF4 had options to adjust your reticle far more advanced than a game released in 2025. Give players the ability to also change the glow intensity and size of their reticles. You have added the colors, you're just missing these. When running, give players an option to switch from the dot reticle to the chevron based off their preference. On 1440p and above the dot is so tiny and hard to see it is ridiculous. Audio: Yet another award for audio design in this game? How, WHY? You can't hear a tank right next to you but you can hear a jet go Mach Jesus from 3 maps away. The footstep audio and the perception of the direction it comes from is insanely bad. Go play BF1, with any headset, with the preset "Logitech G-Pro" and you will immediately tell which BF game had the best audio right away. I'm not sure about you all but I play FPS games to shoot things. How is something as fundamental as footsteps an afterthought with this game and so poorly delivered? All this does is punish players potential and doesn't allow them to make informed decisions with their gameplay. Nerfing movement while simultaneously making guns more of a laser beam than they already were is absurd. Appreciate you all having controller players on 25% less recoil, really neat. /s As it stands now the movement in this game isn't that much ahead of Post-nerf BF1. I've already dealt with the changes they did with BF1 for years and I'll not tolerate additional movement nerfs that didn't need to be made in the first place, I obviously expected changes in some areas but this level of incompetence with BF6 is unacceptable. BF3 run speed was faster than this game. Every BF game that has released with crossplay has had mouse input issues. It seems to be rocket science for developers to either make FPS games separated from PC and Console, or have crossplay with INPUT BASED matching. They say the mouse input is fine but something still feels off with it, anyone who played prior titles and are competent with a mouse should be able to tell this right away. The large majority of console players are just constantly complaining about MnK users and vice versa. Solve this issue, stop making BF games with crossplay or force input based games. Maps: mid at best, some better than others. Lets talk about infantry focused maps for a moment. Some of the best maps designed for infantry gameplay in the entire franchise were on BF1, where are the infantry focused maps on BF6? You all should really reacquire whoever designed these maps for conquest: Achi Baba, Prise de Tahure, Passchendaele, Argonne Forest, Fort de Vaux and even Amiens as overrated and overplayed as that map was. Prise > Amiens. Vehicles: Really cool how there is no penalty for vehicles to sit in their uncap while getting defenses that destroy all incoming fire so they cannot be damaged by anything other than a straight down jet ram. Blackwell Fields is a prime example illustrating this problem. Why have tanks at all on the map if it's up to individuals as a squad to do your teams armor job for them for an entire match, while they sit in their uncap, near un-killable, wasting a vehicle for people that have a W key on their keyboard that would accomplish more trying to take objectives. I am immeasurably disappointed with the people you all chose to listen to and have been listening to since BF1. This game has little to no skill gap in its infantry gameplay, the one thing you all did right was with how suppression works and that carried over from BFV. BF6 lacks depth and long term re-playability. I'm not a vehicle main but any of the incredibly skilled vehicle players from BF3/BF4 will tell you this vehicle skill ceiling in this game is severely lacking. It's pretty simple logic, make the game good first with a skill ceiling and people will adapt. Maybe if you all didn't listen to little Timmy that gets on for a weekend once every blue moon this game would be in a better place. That's exactly what you all did with BF1 and is the reason the movement went to crap on it as well, don't even get me started on the SMG08 buff. Reddit has ruled your decisions and the people that actually play your games long term have no voice and no input, if they have input you ignore it. The reason people played BF2/BF3/BF4 so long was because of a skill gap. Even BF1 had a skill gap despite movement being nerfed into the ground, because the gunplay had depth and the game had the best audio and map design in the entire franchise and before anyone reads this and goes "but Random Bullet Deviation" it doesn't exist in BF1. People confuse spread and suppression and this term was made up by someone that had no clue about what they were talking about. All of these people are not the core BF playerbase, never has been, never will be. You might get sales out of them every other game. And you all expect to go on a yearly release cycle of BF's? LMAO. The lack of tools to run 3rd party servers which you started implementing with BF1 is the biggest mistake you all could have ever made. Communities and community servers are what keeps BF games going. You have to give people a reason to play outside of ranks and that reason is skill gap. Give people something to strive for. Breakthrough/Ops: This game mode, first made an appearance in BF1 and a lot of people loved it, which is fine. However, Breakthrough/Ops is one of the primary reasons people are useless as Conquest players, the core BF experience. Seemingly none of them have bought a keyboard with a W key attached to it or know how to play their class. Previous titles haven't been on sale in 6 months, I chalked it up to new EA ownership when they missed the first major sale. It's pretty clear they want their older games to die and for people to move on to BF6. As a 21 year player of the BF franchise, yesterday I made the decision to permanently quit this franchise. After most of the OG team departed (whom made BF1) you all have lost what made BF games great. You don't need to reinvent the wheel. Off topic: I'd love to post a review of BF1 on steam but you're not allowed to if you own it on Origin/EA, maybe I'll make one on YT, we'll see.

review_text: Yet again, we were fooled into believing that the good ol' Battlefield was back. In reality, the maps are a fraction of what they used to be, the game is flooded with uninspired slop skins, bugs, and questionable design choices nobody seems to have asked for. Back in the BF4 and BF1 era, I used to come home from work and play a couple of rounds with friends, and sometimes even solo. Nowadays, we probably play once or twice a month, and almost every time it feels dreadful. I don't know if it's the close proximity of everything, the COD like movement, the map design, or a combination of all of it, but you are constantly trying to dodge bullets from every possible direction. Crazy, right? I'm complaining about getting shot in a shooter. But the problem isn't simply getting shot. It's getting shot from multiple directions almost all the damn time. Half the matches feel like you're either stomping the other team or getting absolutely stomped yourself. There is barely any middle ground. And don't even get me started on the game modes. They keep adding random modes nobody asked for while removing Rush and TDM. Like, what? Maybe I'm getting old and need to get with the times, but eh. Clearly I'm not the only one who feels this way. The charm isn't there anymore. The immersion isn't there either. Vehicles somehow feel sluggish, while others require an insane amount of practice just to become remotely competent. Take jets. I was never some amazing pilot, but in BF4 and BF1 I could at least hold my own. Here? Nah. Every damn match seems to have one Ace pilot who apparently does nothing besides sit in front of a computer treating Battlefield like a full time job. What are you supposed to do? Grab an AA launcher? Sure. Except half of them feel slow as hell. And the RPG. Oh, how they massacred my boy. They basically got rid of meaningful splash damage on a freaking RPG. Then, even when you land what looks like a perfect hit, half the time the damage doesn't seem to register properly. I genuinely don't understand why the developers are so hell bent on spending time adding pointless crap nobody asked for instead of improving what Battlefield is actually supposed to be good at. All that development time could have gone toward more maps, for Christ's sake. One map every couple of months? My brother in Christ, I am already tired of your "new" map after playing it a handful of times, especially when half the time it's just an old map being remastered again. Battlefield used to be the game I could jump into after work and lose a few hours in without even noticing. Now I play two rounds and I'm already wondering why the hell I launched it.

review_text: I played the beta and loved every second of it. When it ended, I could not think of anything else -it was just me and other Battlefield diehards, living the dream. The campaign is not bad, but it is nowhere near the immersion of Battlefield 3 or 4. The character designs feel a bit off; the skins lack detail, and no one really stands out as an iconic figure worth remembering. Often rigged with bugs or just distracting assets disappearing in thin air, like a vehicle you just blew up might disappear shortly after, same with corpses from your enemies. I also fell through the map after getting out of a military vehicle. The AI feels very brain-dead; they often stand there, doing nothing. Same with friendly AI. They are not coded to kill enemies for you unless you order them to. So, a lot of the time, I was getting flanked by the enemy when I thought everything was clear, because my teammates were not reacting to anything. But they were ignoring an enemy standing right where I wanted to take cover, and they had a clear view of it the whole time. Happens a lot. The multiplayer, though... oh boy. Gameplay feels great, but the netcode is still awful at times. You can empty half a mag into someone’s skull and they just shrug it off, then two-tap you without a single muzzle flash. review_text: This review is borne out of genuine frustration. Anti-teamplay: It encourages players to farm specific stats rather than playing the objective. Anti-fun: The process is boring and repetitive. DICE, you must revisit these challenges. Dial back the required numbers significantly. Stop trying to force a ludicrous grind for attachments. If the goal is player retention, this system is a spectacular failure. Right now, it feels less like a game and more like a second job, and that is not what Battlefield should be. Do better, please.

review_text: Battlefield 6 has some fun moments The core gunplay can be enjoyable, and the casual modes are entertaining, especially since the AI bots often play the objective surprisingly well. The visuals are also impressive, and Battlefield still delivers those signature large-scale moments that the series is known for. That said, I ran into several issues that kept me from fully enjoying the game. Crossplay balance is my biggest concern. Controller aim assist, particularly on consoles, feels very strong from a PC perspective. Many engagements felt like I was fighting against extremely accurate tracking, regardless of whether the opponent was using a sniper rifle or a pistol. Whether it's perfectly balanced or not, it often feels frustrating as a mouse and keyboard player. The maps also feel quite small for the current weapon balance. SMGs are effective at surprisingly long ranges, which leads to fast-paced matches with very little downtime or tactical positioning. Movement is extremely fast, making battles feel more like constant close-quarters action than the slower, strategic Battlefield experience I was hoping for. I've also seen increasing discussion around third-party controller adapters that allegedly enhance aim assist or vehicle controls. Even if not everyone uses them, their presence raises concerns about competitive integrity. Performance could be better. Even on high-end PC hardware capable of well over 200 FPS, the game doesn't always feel as smooth as the frame rate suggests. There are noticeable stutters and optimization issues that take away from the experience. The single-player campaign is short, taking roughly four hours to finish, and I didn't find it particularly memorable. Monetization is another weak point. The store is packed with cosmetic bundles, progression can be accelerated through purchases, and it sometimes feels like spending money is encouraged more than simply playing the game. I also had a confusing experience purchasing Battlefield Pro twice, once directly and once using Battlefield Coins, and my duplicate purchase wasn't refunded. Finally, moderation feels overly strict when it comes to chat. Players can receive lengthy chat bans for relatively minor language, while it often feels like more significant issues don't receive the same level of attention. Overall: Battlefield 6 still has exciting moments and can be fun with friends, but as a PC player I came away disappointed by the crossplay balance, map design, optimization, monetization, and moderation. If these areas improve over time, my opinion could certainly change, but in its current state I find it difficult to recommend to players looking for a polished PC Battlefield experience. That said, I genuinely hope the developers continue improving the game. Battlefield has always been one of my favorite franchises, and I'd love to see Battlefield 6 become the experience it has the potential to be. If DICE listens to player feedback, improves PC optimization, fine-tunes crossplay balance, and focuses on fair competition, I'll gladly revisit my review in the future. I want this game to succeed, because at its core, Battlefield still has something special.

review_text: Battlefield 6 was marketed as allowing players to 'play their own way' and could earn full XP/progress unlocks from playing community experiences via Portal - this is no longer the case as of the date of this review. In an attempt to resolve Bot farming in Portal, Battlefield Studios have made amendments to the back-end of the game which has resulted in Portal's Official Experience / Community Experience servers no longer awarding players with full XP / complete progression. This means that you can no longer complete assignments and challenges for unlocks (such as weapons, equipment, cosmetic appearances), which means zero progression whatsoever. The only way to earn full XP / complete progression is to play on 'official servers', which usually does not allow back-filling via bots - meaning that if you're playing in off-peak hours (Oceanic servers especially) you are less likely to find matches, and be unable to play the game as intended. This doesn't really bode well for the games future.

review_text: I am a BF4 and BF3 fan. BF1 was good, it dropped off after 5, and I didn't touch 2042. There is greatness here... just needs to be unlocked. Hit registration is as close to RNG as it can be. When you shoot, multiple bullets are sent in packets and not recognized individually. The game then tries to determine how much you hit instead of you just actually hitting your target. I have jumped around a corner, mag dumb at 5m, and score 50pts of damage. The guy turns and kills me. I have seen enemies blitz me, getting the jump on me, and leave me sitting fine while I gun them down. I have had enemies shoot me as I am standing still, only for me to turn and kill them. On top of this, the bloom is inconsistent. The way to attempt to beat this is tap fire. Tap fire sends out several packets instead of 1 which increases your probability of hit. This makes fast firing, close range weapons king at all ranges. I have used the same gun with camo and without camo, using the same attachments, and 1 performs worse than the other. It is weird janky stuff. I also suggest not believing all the attachments. Use the firing range top figure out if it actually changes it or not... you'd be surprised what actually happens. The bugs are pretty minimal, but there are a few major ones. - In the menus where you cant select attachments - In the challenges where things just don't count - Not getting XP for repairing - No one is getting healed for healing challenges Good basis, the Beta was great past the movement, when this stuff changes, I will edit my review. EDIT 11/04 Some strides have been made in the right direction. Gun play is getting better. I will edit further as we go but packet issues are still considerably there. I think if they can find a way to ever-so-slightly slow the pace of the game down would be helpful too. EDIT 12/23 Minor fixes have been applied... its battlefield... just not BATTLEFIELD. Too much grind, weird issues. I don't think I can recommend it. It is better than some of the others, but BF3, BF4, & BF1 were so great... I just wish se could have that again EDIT 7/4 Came back after season 3 to check it out. Having some fun... Lot of steps in the right direction. I am excited to see this new naval stuff. Challenges still a bit grindy, weapons definitely take too long to get attachments. I miss BF4... EDIT 8/23 I have had fun with the game and much has been improved, but it still a movement shooter with over complicated attachments and the most ridiculous grind. Even bot lobbies aren't enough

review_text: I’ve been playing Battlefield for a very long time, starting with the early entries of the series, and really getting into it properly from Bad Company onward. BF6 is a good game overall, but a lot of what it offers has been done before. Destruction was already a big part of Bad Company 2, BF3, and especially BF4. That’s always been what Battlefield meant to me: large maps, a certain level of destruction, and environmental effects like floods or severe weather. To me, Battlefield feels like it’s constantly moving back and forth — one step forward, then one step back. I understand that it’s difficult to please every type of player. Still, Battlefield was always Battlefield to me, and Call of Duty was Call of Duty. In the past, the communities could hardly stand each other. Today, however, players on both sides are starting to wonder what the publishers are actually doing with these two franchises as the games become more and more alike.

review_text: Game isn't worthy of "GOY" Game isn't Battlefield. It does not play like a Battlefield. It does not feel nor resemble one. It carries the audio, it carries part of the UI. But movement, gun play, balance, mechanics are all modern adaptions to what made the former titles great. It is not a rebirth, nor a revival. It is a synthetic imitation designed by recently hired developers. BattleField 6 is what happens when you ask todays developers, to create a game that resembles older titles, but with modern spins to it. It cannot capture what made the former titles great because it is attempting to grasp at the new players. Not the core audiance of the former titles. And with new devs, it carries their ideas and motives. As well as the backers and financers. I look at BattleField 1 on my libary and know with out doubt if I want to get on I can have fun. I know if I click play and hop on I will have some good matches the way I want to play. But here? The game, as all have stated. Even since beta. This game trys too hard to be Call of Duty, it is an appeal to the modern gamer, to the modern Streamers and content creators. I look to Battlefield 6, and I don't have that feeling. I don't have that "I know I will have fun" feeling. I look to Battlefield 6, and go "I wanna play because I paid money for it. Not because I want to have fun." And that doesn't spark joy, but spite and resentment. I know I boot BF1 jump in a lobby for a late night game. And will get off having some fun atleast as a machine gunner. Battlefield 6? Small maps to keep you engaged enough to die, spawn, die, spawn. Maps are not destructive, but pre-slective destruction. Alot of maps then suffer due to this and they become Lane maps like MMO. Where you funnel people into 3-4 lanes. And add a good team with vehicles and it becomes 1 sided many times. LMG's are useless because there is no suppression. Snipers are uncounterable nor a problem. A good sniper can counter sniper and kill infantry on their way to kill said sniper. A sniper has no counter play unless you are a better sniper, or you involve a vehicle or drive up to them with a truck. But you can't do that all the time, and most maps have over lapping situations. You can't fly a heli as half the enemy team will be engineers waiting for anything to shoot a rocket at, you can't go tank because you'll be lit up with RPG's. You can't rush or flank to the sniper because they have a drone spotting you, let alone they can spot you and you have to wave though the whole enemy team. Gun fights devolve into who shoots faster, who shoots fast and has better spray control. Thus, LMG's lose out to SMG"s even at long range as the LMG loses accuracy past 2 shots fired. This game was created with Battle Royal first, and the core game secondary. The next "huge map" is a massive golf corse that screams "I'm a warzone map". review_text: The game has an okay base — it’s Battlefield — but the design feels weak. The maps are boring and the balance is pretty bad. On some maps you get shot down right after taking off. And the amount of vehicles on each map feels random: too many on some maps, almost none on others. Ground vehicles aren’t fun. The Bradley has only two useful seats, tanks feel empty, and older Battlefield games had much better vehicle gameplay. Weapon leveling and skins are a huge grind. It takes forever and doesn’t feel worth it. The interface looks almost copied from Call of Duty. Even if that style was popular in CoD, it doesn’t mean Battlefield should just take it. The game loses individuality because of it. The new Redsec mode (their Battle Royale) also feels weird. Releasing a Battle Royale in 2025 feels like the trend is long gone. And the gameplay looks so much like Call of Duty that sometimes you don’t even know what game you’re in. It feels like they put a lot of effort into Redsec instead of fixing balance, making better maps, or improving vehicle systems. Another problem is the weapons themselves. It feels like none of them really stand out. Most guns feel almost the same, just with slightly different stats. There’s no weapon that makes you think, “Yeah, I really want to play with this.” If you think back to Battlefield 1, the guns had crazy personality — fast-firing LMGs with huge recoil, bolt-action rifles, all kinds of different playstyles. Sure, the setting was different, but the gameplay was way more interesting and varied. In this Battlefield, the shotguns are actually fun, and running around with them is cool... but that’s basically it. There are some good points. The attack helicopter is fun to use. The first-person free look is great. And the transport helicopter guns are finally strong, so gunners can actually get kills. But overall, nothing really stands out. It’s just a basic shooter. The new revive animation is okay, but doesn’t change much. The core is fine, but the design is weak.

review_text: What can I say? I'm stupid, and I bought this game hoping it would be anything like BF1. It's not. I loved everything about that game and, as far as shooter games go, I've never played its equal. In BF1, you are in the battle; you feel the explosions and you become totally immersed in your environment. Immediately upon playing I realized this game was nothing like BF1. The best way to describe the difference in game-feel between the two titles is that BF1 feels like you're looking through your screen at another world—playing BF6 feels like you're doing EA a favor. Never forget: EA is a soulless corporation that clearly spends less effort on development than it spends marketing husks of our favorite franchises to us in the form of quarter-baked, hollow "games." We have taught the executives of this company that we will buy anything as long as there is enough hype. I am done with the BS. Never in my life will I purchase another game from this publisher until there is a palpable, fundamental shift in their business strategy. I will leave you with EA's own description of their business practices: "We create stories and deliver amazing experiences that resonate with audiences around the world and make an impact in the communities where we live, work and play." You tell me: has EA had a net positive or net negative impact on your life in the last decade? Has this corporation delivered more amazing or poor experiences to audiences in the last decade? Does EA care about resonating with audiences around the world? I refuse to fund the marketing of your next overhyped POS game. Please consider joining me in boycotting this publisher.

review_text: Look, I just want to be honest with you all. I know it's not the same Battlefield as before, especially after Battlefield 1, 4, or Hardline. Each new game will be different, but I will say this: Battlefield is fun, and I found myself a little addicted to it when I bought it during the summer sales. If you really love Battlefield and have lost trust in the franchise due to what happened with Battlefield 2042, I understand. However, I promise you the game is enjoyable and works well. I haven’t experienced any significant bugs so far. The maps are decent, and the classes and weapons are fun to use. Playing with friends in squads enhances the experience because good communication makes the game even better. You don’t necessarily need to be on a call; even random players can often work together effectively. Overall, I find the game enjoyable, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who loves Battlefield but struggles to trust the series after the issues with Battlefield 2042. One thing to note is that there aren’t any crazy skins like COD. There is a battle pass, but it’s not a big deal; you can enjoy the game without it. There is a battle royale mode, but I personally don’t like battle royale games, I tried it once and didn’t enjoy it much. I haven’t noticed many negatives, but one thing I will mention is that there aren’t many secondary weapons available. The gadgets are good, but the challenges to unlock items for your classes can be tough. For example, to upgrade the engineer class, you need to use launchers and motion sensors launchers. I forgot the name. The one challenge I really disliked was for the support class, where you have to get 25 assist kills in smoke, which was quite frustrating. In summary, I think the game is really fun, and I highly recommend giving it a shot. Play for about an hour or two, and if you don’t like it, you can return it. Yes, I know it’s a bit pricey, but you might want to wait for a sale or go ahead and buy it if you’re a fan of Battlefield. I hope the game continues to run well and that a player base remains as the community grows.

review_text: The first two weeks of this game showed real promise for the future of Battlefield. However, with the release of Season 1 it has become clear that BF6 is not a return to form but simply a means for EA and DICE to use the Battlefield name to sell cosmetics for the new BR mode. The promises of grounded warfare in destructible maps has proven to be false with maps that are compact and poorly designed. Even more blatant is the design of the Season 1 skins that feel more at home in Warzone or BF 2042 than the suppose original vision of BF6. The core gameplay of BF6 is enjoyable and has the potential to be brilliant, but the indications are that BF6 is NOT meant for Battlefield fans of old, instead it is more akin to Call of Duty which isn't inherently bad, but it isn't Battlefield.

review_text: Obviously, the game is not optimized at all and still runs like garbage, despite the game not even being all that pretty and the overall artstyle is kinda bland since they went with a ""realistic"" approach. 2nd flaw, that I think is way bigger and can't even really be fixed with ascendance, is that the areas just aren't really all that readable or fun to traverse in any way. I guess the first area is ok since it's just a giant open desert and field with some caves, but everything after that is just so labyrinthine and hard to explore. You start to understand why they added auto movement with the Seikret, and it's because all the areas are just huge pains in the butt to explore and a lot of areas just have very few landmarks to help memorize the maps. I never had this issue with World, Rise, GU, 4U or 3U. Wound system is kinda interesting, but I feel the execution is kinda poor since it just pauses all action to do some attack for some free damage and most weaker monster just get juggled by this mechanic, meaning the only real threats are the larger monsters. I get that you feel strong and badass when doing it, but it seems like a waste to just fully trivialize half the roster. Otherwise, the fights against the later game monsters are genuinely pretty fun, particularly like mizu, but I hope to god G-rank Lagia removes that dumbass minigame that happens at the end of the fight(temu a*s swimming combat). I dunno, this game just feels kinda weak overall. wait for when ascendance comes out and see if it actually makes any big fixes.

review_text: I love Monster Hunter. I have over 200 hours each in Rise and Generations Ultimate and a more modest amount in World, which makes it hurt to not recommend this game. But even after the supposed performance improvements, it runs badly, and the worst part is that the frame timings basically oscillate, which makes me nauseous. I used to play on a ♥♥♥ gaming laptop, so I can tolerate low frame rates, but the stuttering and erratic frame times make me straight up nauseous. The core combat is as fun as ever, and I think this is one of the best iterations of the Dual Blades. Everything around it is what sucks. The story sucks ass (okay, all Monster Hunter stories suck), but this is by far the worst one, and it's the one that puts the story most front and center. There are a bunch of 10+ minute slow-walking sequences. The awful cutscenes are at least skippable, but the walking sequences are not. The characters go "wow, look how beautiful these butterflies are" and the camera does a 15-second zoom on them. This happens dozens of times. It feels like the developers didn't trust me to experience this world and find it beautiful on my own. It's patronizing, and ironically it hurts the enjoyment of the game a lot. And while the game runs like ♥♥♥, it also looks flat and just not that good. The animations are top notch like in every Monster Hunter game, and Arkveld's chains probably have more polygons than all of GenU. But the color grading looks awful, random textures look completely flat and are much lower resolution than the rest of the game, and the art style just doesn't do it for me. It might be far more technically impressive than Rise, but Rise looks better to me, and it runs at playable frame rates. They spent a huge amount of time and effort building a massive world that the Seikret's auto-run makes completely irrelevant. I have no incentive to explore it, which isn't helped by the performance. The QoL from Rise is basically gone. Things that took 2 button presses now take 5 to 10 for no reason. The combat is still fun, but literally everything else is some of the worst in any Monster Hunter game I've played. If you think you can tolerate the performance and everything around the combat, which the game for some reason keeps you away from as much as it can, go ahead. Everyone else, stay away.

review_text: For a player who have just start the series in World, I personally think that this is a great improvement from World. I have played World for roughly 370 hours, i don't considered myself veteran to the game but there's a lot of thing i really like about Wilds, I like how the slinger aiming is improve by a lot, its just auto lock if you did click the thing you want to collect, there's mount that you could use in many ways and it is great live saver in a lot of time, and it make you able to whetstone your weapon while mounting. Focus mode is a REALLY REALLY GREAT addition, its a new mechanic into the game and it really help a lot, you will actually face the monster the way your cam face toward and its allow you to see wounded part, shoot slinger and is a lot better than monster locking system. Ofc there's also things that I think still need to change like how bad the difficulties change around late game, and how short the main story line ends in base game, in World it will take you around 20 hrs to complete the story first time or less than that but it still be at least 10 hrs for first time, In Wilds that took like 8 to 12 hrs to complete the whole story line and there's no master rank yet which also shorten the content for me at least. Lastly although the game didn't turn out perfect, the performance issues for older gens pc (which make me un-able to play with my friends) if they gonna choose to optimize the performance seriously it could have been better, yes i know its a lot better now bc i was there too when the Beta Test came out but theres still room for improvement, and i think better to just wait for DLC to came out before buying this. I know yall won't read all that and probably scroll down, so here the summary; Just wait for the DLC, the game is good just wait for the DLC.

review_text: Such a wonderful version, with many improvements over previous ones. This Wilds version provides "mantles" (additional equipment that supports players by allowing them to evade or become immune to certain monster effects) for new players, instead of requiring them to complete numerous annoying side quests as before. On the other hand, when players have filled all the slots in their pouches, this version allows them to collect additional items and store them in their inventory instead. The Focus Mode (better switched from Hold to Toggle) allows us to target vulnerable parts to weaken monsters, which is another wonderful improvement in this version. Besides, recent updates have already fixed the annoying performance issues. The Medium/Low graphics settings combined with Balanced/Performance mode work best for me, with no issues at all.

review_text: this game is kind of bad. my opinion may change later on when the dlc, ascendance, releases. as it stands now the game is very poorly optimized, quite easy in comparison to older games, and the story is very overbearing. spoiler free section: the monsters are mostly returning monsters and are nerfed to be slower and feel like they take turns when you fight them. the story is quite overbearing and will force you to walk where they want you to go at the spped they say you should and you have to watch as the characters stop the game to tell you exactly whats happening and what they think about it. the game is also very poorly optimized i get fairly consistent 60fps until i engage with certain monsters and they drop it as low as 7fps. if you want to play a monster hunter game i have a few recommendations for you: if you want an easier game that feels unique and a higher speed game, play mh rise; if you want a more hunting focused game with heavy work into the environment, play mh world; if you want a harder more authentic experience that makes you actually have to learn what you are doing play either mh3u or mh4u. spoilers maybe: the monster i listed earlier that drops frames like a rock is sergios. the monsters like the tempered guardian ebony odogaron feel like how a regular odogaron used to. i hate nata. i have played old mh games for a very long time since my grandma got me mh3 for the wii when i was like 6 and i have loved it ever since but this is a disgrace to the previous games. i hate nata. its a worse worldbuilding experience than world as there are so few monsters and the people act as they havent imagined a weapon before. please remove nata. you specifically are followed by this chick named alma who if i didnt know better would assume she works for peta. why is this entire economy held up by one hunter? why in the later parts like the gore magala fight do i nee/d assistance? why is the sekreit so broken and overpowered? also why did you change the cooking steaks? i miss the old bbq spit and the cooking minigame. also why does making a steak make so many steaks? im going to stop here but there are many many small things that make this game feel so corporate and soulless in comparison to what i know capcom can do and has done before.

review_text: The game is fun. Performance could be better (I average around 80 fps on mostly medium settings). It is believed it will be improved with the release of the Ascendance expansion. In my ~50 hours of playing the game has crashed twice, neither of which happened at critical moments during hunts or cutscenes so I'm not too beat up about it. I got the base game for like $24 USD, definitely worth the price for me. As someone who is relatively new to the series (having played Rise and World), this feels like a good evolution for the series gameplay wise. You could argue focus mode is maybe a little too forgiving with positioning, but honestly, I think its just a fun mechanic that allows you to hit the monster more consistently. If you're a purist about it you can just not use it.

review_text: The "not recommended" comes not from any issues with the game, combat design, or performance. I quite love offset attacks and wounds, I love the additions to the movesets of many weapons, not particularly bothered by the self-driving mounts, don't really have performance issues either. My specs (as seen below) surprisingly get me a fairly stable 60 fps (with like 50 fps lows at worst) most of the time at 1440p ultrawide on mostly max settings (no raytracing, FSR upscaling, no framegen, but lowered volumetrics and foliage). The game looks pretty enough (though not quite deserving of the hardware requirements), and the fashion is probably the best I've experienced in the games I've played (world and sunbreak). My issue comes entirely from the GPU crashing that many people also experience. I've tried every single solution proposed (except for fully reinstalling windows, I'm not doing that for certain reasons), and nothing has been able to remedy the issue. At best I've obtained slightly more stability, but it's hard to estimate, as the game will sometimes crash every 30-50 minutes, or I might go an entire day with no issues. Going through a harder hunt, only for the game to crash just as the monster is about to die, or worse - on the reward screen right before the game saves, is really off-putting. And when you need to grind a fair amount, especially if you want to play a variety of weapons, the frustration adds up really quickly. I've at least gotten my money's worth, but I cannot recommend the game when there's a decent chance of having an unsolvable crashing issue.

review_text: I've been holding off reviewing this game for a couple of reasons. Most people will know by now that PC performance of the game has been pretty bad for all but the most recent hardware. And even then it still has issues. Truth be told though, it's not that interesting of an issue to me. Beyond the fact that I have recent hardware and have never had any major problems running the game, the dumb reality of "AAA" gaming is that everything it broken and gets patched up later. So I decided to wait and see what kinds of patching they would do. And we're finally finding out... a year later... when the base game is at end of life. It looks like the bulk of what they're doing is adding more options to reduce or disable features which eat up CPU processing power. Now this I care about. Because it entails something about the development. It entails that they jammed their game full of these CPU hogging "features" without any concern for how they would impact the game. Which is exactly what you would do if you were using your game as a tool to incentivize people to buy new hardware. And oh! Look. Wilds codes came "free" with a lot of the latest PC hardware. I had suspected that this was the case for a long time. But the devs are tacitly confirming it now. They blew up their game with tons of processor chewing "high fidelity" features and knew that it would come at the expense of the game looking bad for anyone who wasn't on the latest and greatest hardware. This is simply unacceptable behavior. Making your game worse to prey on the insecurity of your playerbase for profit is immoral and bad design. So, there simply is no recourse here. This is a bad game. The devs do not respect you or the game enough to treat it as anything other than a cynical cash grab. You should not pay money for this game. No amount of updates or performance improvements will ever change that. If the devs don't respect you, there's no reason to respect them. And all of that is before even factoring in my actual critique of the game. Redundant systems. Half baked features which only exist for the sake of feature bloat. An absolutely insane difficulty progression which is shaped more like a climate change graph than a game progression. Stilted weapon redesigns with clear winners and losers. Weapons losing core aspects of their identity. The skill ceiling for the game being lowered. The "festivals" which exist primarily to sell you new DLC. The list goes on and on. There are things I like about it too. But the issue is that there's nothing positive I can say which does not require some kind of qualification or backhanded compliment. The 9 Star monsters are good. But they should have been the 8 Star monsters and they shouldn't only exist as a result of player backlash to how easy the game was. See what I mean? Good things which only exist in relation to something bad. That's the whole game. I would struggle to recommend this to anyone who wasn't already a die hard fan. And, given the whole argument laid out at the beginning, I could certainly never recommend that someone lay down seventy dollars for it. Monster Hunter Wilds is a massive disappointment on multiple fronts. You can play it. You can even have fun doing so. But that's true of most games. You'd be better off spending your time and money on games built out of love for the medium and respect for the player. Monster Hunter Wilds is just cynicism manifest. I see no reason to reward this behavior and no reason why you should either.

review_text: I bought the Premium Deluxe Edition because I wanted to support the game, only to receive around 20% of the DLC that has been released. Even though the game has always had optimization issues that made my PC struggle, and despite the muddy graphics, I continued to support it because I genuinely enjoyed the game. I never left a negative review because I believed in what the developers were building. That's why the new Gold Edition feels like a slap in the face to early supporters. New players can now buy the base game and all the DLC for a much better price, while those of us who supported the game from day one paid full price for the game and the DLC over time. What's even more disappointing is that there are no meaningful loyalty discounts for existing owners. Even after already owning the Premium Deluxe Edition and purchasing some of the DLC separately, we'd still have to pay almost full price to get everything included in the Gold Edition. Loyal players who supported the game from the beginning should be rewarded, not end up paying the most for the least value. My advice to anyone considering buying this game: don't buy it right now. Wait until it's heavily discounted or until a complete edition is available. You'll get a far better deal than the players who supported the game from day one.
