review_text: A very cool experiment in game design, From treads new ground in the most efficient way possible, reusing large numbers of Elden Ring assets and reconfiguring them into a completely new experience. A little bit like a roguelike, a little bit like a battle royale, Nightreign has you racing against the clock trying to become as powerful as possible across two days before the showdown with the Nightlord on the third day. Defeating the challenge requires you to figure out a route through the semi-randomized map on the fly, avoiding powerful enemies until you've leveled up, hunting down ruins holding weapons with the boss's weakness, deciding whether you're better off going to a mine to upgrade your weapon or going to a high level fight to hope a better weapon drops. Each playable character is similar to a build you might create for an Elden Ring playthrough, but with a set of unique skills and passives that suit that role -- The dedicated caster has an ability that lets her recover spellpower and concoct new spells based on elemental residue, the greatsword warrior has a grappling hook that lets him quickly move in and out of combat range, the hulking tank has an ability that lets him briefly ignore damage and create a massive counterattack. Each character feels very distinctive, much more so than an Elden Ring playthrough, and having to improvise with what you find gives an opportunity to experiment with weapons and spells you'd never touch on such a playthrough. It's not for everyone, the relentless pace can be difficult to get used to, but I think this experiment is a resounding success.

review_text: It's addictingly fun and one of my favorite games I can't put down. It takes the gameplay of Souls games and adds fluid movement to the combat and I find myself having trouble going back to play ER due to how slow it feels now. The gameplay loop is fun and there's plenty of variance in each run, despite there being only 2 maps (yes, the shifting earths are variants of the 1st map, but there's SO many locations across the Souls series they could pull from, as they've shown from the selection of bosses). It's much more fun playing multiplayer. My biggest criticism is easily the relic system. Yes, it's a great idea and it makes for some fun builds and even more varied gameplay, but there's only 2 ways of obtaining decent relics, aside from some decent story ones: 1) playing matches and obtaining relics based on how far you went/if you cleared the nightlord. 2) a gacha-like store. And after spending millions rolling in the store, I can personally tell you the drop rates for actual good rolls is abysmal. It's no wonder why double Balancers has been the meta since the DLC dropped; aside from it resulting in some insane damage numbers on certain characters, it alleviates the main issue of the game of not having good relics to build around. The build variety in this game through the relic system makes for a very fun experience and it's a shame that it's severely hindered by tying the system to pure RNG. Even so. I'll see you all in-game. Gotta protect the flock, y'know?

review_text: I'm going to leave this review for those who are like me who love Elden Ring, but might still be on the fence about Nightreign. This is nothing at all like Shadow of the Erdtree or Vanilla. It's more of a spinoff than a real souls game. Nightreign is a wonderful game for people who enjoy boss rushes/gauntlets, speedrunning, or practicing and refining a plan many times over to perfection. It is fine-tuned to be a dream game for people just like this. It can also be a good activity for people to play a quick pickup game with some friends, since one expedition takes roughly only half an hour, depending on how strong the team is. Nightreign is a hard pass for people who like exploration, world design, "play at your own pace", slow boss fights using inefficient meme builds, or dungeon style beat-em-up combat over bosses. You will be punished for doing any of this. Nightreign expects players to be on edge the moment they begin an expedition. You don't have time to read prompts, look at descriptions, test out weapons, or explore non-meta paths if you aren't already moving to another boss area. The fortnite circle closes incredibly fast and you need to be leveling and gearing up as fast as possible to stay ahead. If you fall behind, there is no catchup. You will be behind the rest of the expedition. Sites of grace automatically levels your character stats. You use sites of grace as checkpoints to run through, rather than as bonfires for resting. The gameplay loop is like this: Drop in, Run to the nearest basic enemy (rats or hollows), kill them, run to the nearest site of grace, spam the action key to level up, run to the nearest encampment or easy field boss, level up at a site of grace, repeat until day 3. Note that every other basic enemy should be outright ignored for the rest of the game. Fighting them is inefficient and spending too much time on them will cause you to fall behind. I'm honestly not sure why they're even included in the game. We all run past them 100% of the time because we have to. If you're thinking that must be some tryhard speedrunning optimization, its not. It's nearly mandatory to do it this way for every expedition. This game is all about boss fights. Clearing field bosses as fast as you possibly can so that you have better odds of beating the night lord boss. This is Nightreign in a nutshell. With all that being said, I will at least give them credit that I really enjoyed the inclusion of bosses from past souls games. There are tons of easter eggs and references to DS1 and even DS2. It's just such a shame that I really can't tell you much else about the game, because the game encourages you to run past everything and go to the next boss. I don't even remember the designs of a lot of areas in the map (like random events and shifting earth maps). But I can tell you where to pick up another flask at a church ruin, i guess. The negatives outweigh the positives for me.

review_text: I want to like it. The core of an enjoyable game is there. But this is the sweatiest Fromsoft entry ever made and every individual part of that sweatiness is bad on its own merits. - Random drop based relic power up system. Requires you to farm away hours of your life on a random drop system that is honestly abjectly terrible. Most relics are useless for any character. Plenty of buffs are situational at best and managing relics is absolute ♥♥♥ overall if they expect people to manage different relic setups and large numbers of relics. - Putting a challenging boss behind a 45 minute playthrough with no way to practice it only works for one type of player. If you dont have good reflexes and have to learn the boss rather than natively dodging attacks on your first try, this game is punishingly hard. - Doing most of most characters life bars in damage in a single hit is not hard. Its lazy. The damage scale in this game starts bad and gets worse. Dying with flasks left because you never got a chance to use them because a boss combo one or two shot you is an extremely common occurrence. review_text: It runs and plays like Elden Ring (literally) but in a form of a rogue-like spin-off. It is focused on faster gameplay and online co-op. Nightreign takes 95% of its of weapons, spells and enemy types from base Elden Ring so playing that game first allows you to adapt much faster as you'll know ahead how things work. You start each run (expedition) by picking one of 8 (10 with DLC) pre-made characters, there's solo, duo and 3 player party matchmaking options. Each of them takes you on a ~40 min expeditions where you have to survive 2 days and defeat a night lord at the end. Each expedition has semi-randomized gear drops, points of interest and dynamic events. Combat system is the same like in Elden Ring with addition of new faster sprint (that removes the need for mount) and ability to climb walls. Between the expeditions you collect murk (currency) that you can spend on obtaining new relics (passive bonuses) or outfits for the characters. The plot is as basic as it can be and serves mostly as a background for the gameplay loop. If you just want to play as one character and see the ending credits, the game should take you around 10-15 hours if you succeed most of your expeditions on first attempt. After you complete the story you'll unlock expeditions against stronger versions of most of the bosses as well as "endless night" mode where expeditions get progressively more difficult with each their but you also unlock new slots for build customisation and can find gear with new types of passives and modifiers. If you enjoy the core gameplay-loop, you can easily get hundreds of hours of content out of this game. I highly recommend it (but also I'm biased towards FROMSOFTWARE games) for people who like action-combat rogue-likes and those who want more of Elden Ring after completing it.

review_text: ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN is an MMORPG roguelike designed for players who love leveling characters and adapting their strategies to dramatic environmental changes in every single run. The combat is intense, driven by various types of monsters, tight time limits and equipment variety Unlike traditional Souls games, you can’t rely on a specific loadout all the time because the RNG always forces you to change equipment which affects your playstyle. However, you can use gem slots obtained the shop or after finishing run to add new traits that benefit your build and make your runs much more consistent. While most of the monster return from previous Souls games, they have been adapted perfectly to the game’s mechanics. The community generally knows how to execute a solid run, so there is no need to worry about teammates. If you are new, they will pin the map, lead the way and share loot. Co-op is spectacular, especially with friends, but playing solo is a great option as well. The game scales the monster down specifically how they engage and allow you buy Grace which allows you to gain extra self-revives for each day. The story is excellent if you pay attention to the character quests, which reward you with skins, gems, and journal where the lore is told. There are dialogues and scenes to help you understand the world setting, Niightfarers, other elements that go beyond just rushing bosses. The soundtrack cannot be ignored. It is beautifully designed and fits the game’s theme in every aspect. For instance, the hype goes sky-high during the flights. System requirement aren’t very high. My five-year-old budget laptop still runs it fine, except for the “Baron” boss which directly attacks the CPU. The DLC is also worth it. It meets all my points above and offers more challenges. Even though it isn’t free like the Everdark bosses, the DLC is worth the price for the additional experience in the new underground Limvied and old Limvied. Overall, ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN executes marvelously in all aspects and is worth your money and time.

review_text: This game has a weird enjoyment curve. First it's fun as you learn routes and bosses and optimize your runs. You get to see a lot of older fromsoft bosses and it can feel like a nostalgia victory lap. You get all the bosses down, all of them being some degree of fun. Then you start realizing how awful the relic drop system is. This is managed to a degree by boss relics which tend to be pretty decent, but to get the better ones you need to defeat everdark bosses, and these are a very mixed bag, with some of them being just straight up awful bosses (ED Libra, ED Augur). Not to mention the 45 minute run back to those bosses. You somehow put up with this and see all the content the game has to offer before venturing into the depths. The depths are the worst way of making content harder because it's purely a % adjustment. Enemies just hit harder and have more HP. No different movesets, and the reward pool has even more RNG built into it. It makes the feast or famine aspect way more proeminent, except the fact that when you lose, you lose the equivalent points of 2-3 wins, which just feels extremely punishing. To get the best experience out of this game, play it with friends, beat the normal bosses and some everdark ones, and then stop playing. Even at $40, the game feels a bit overpriced for that amount of content. Also, in typical fromsoft fashion, the game has more than a few bugs and clunkiness, which can end up costing you the run.

review_text: 5 Point review 5 pros and 5 cons. Thumbs up or down is just my personal like or dislike of the game. Pro Insanely replayable from builds, characters, relics you will find something you like or can focus on. All the exclusive bosses to this game are unique and varied and each has a harder version with new moves or phases. Relic system while tedious to get going adds tremendous depth to the game. The shifting system adds variety to maps good and bad but can be selected or changed in game after conditions are met. Co op tends to ruin boss fights in other fromsoft titles but here it feels needed and decently balanced. Con Some of the reused content is either poorly balanced or brain dead compared to other content. Barely anything is explained and some info like scaling cannot be seen during a run and no timer for when the ring closes. Many of the buffs/modifiers are so little or pointless that they just make getting proper builds more rng. relic system using rng to reroll without a locking system(saving one stat rerolling rest) becomes insanely painful. Solo play is just poor in this.
